🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 Rift within Congress: Rajmohan Unnithan challenges Shafi Parambil to public debate, warns ‘teacher and disciple will be exposed’

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 05:13:49 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Unnithan said he was ‘ready to end his political career' if Shafi Parambil could prove that his allegations were baseless

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Intensifying the internal conflict within the Congress in Keralam, Kasaragod MP Rajmohan Unnithan on Tuesday launched a sharp attack on fellow party leader Shafi Parambil, MP, alleging that a coordinated cyber campaign was being orchestrated against him and warning that he would expose those behind it if the attacks continued. Challenging Mr. Parambil to an open public debate, Mr Unnithan said he was “ready to end his political career” if Mr Parambil could prove that his allegations were baseless. He also claimed that he had recorded all relevant details in his personal diary and warned that the people involved, whom he described as “the teacher and the disciple”, would eventually be exposed. Mr Unnithan dismissed the claim that Mr. Parambil belonged to the ‘A’ group in the Congress, saying it would be “the eighth wonder of the world” to describe him as an A group leader. He clarified that he had not insulted Mr Parambil but had only stated that he did not belong to the group. Taking aim at those invoking the legacy of the late former Chief Minister Oommen Chandy, Mr Unnithan said many Congress leaders had stayed away when Chandy was being targeted, while others were concerned about protecting the public image. He questioned where those now speaking about the “Oommen Chandy school of politics” had been at the time. He also maintained that he had not received any personal benefits in Chandy’s name. Mr Unnithan alleged that the social media attacks against him were being conducted through fake accounts as part of a deliberate campaign rather than being spontaneous criticism. He claimed that the operation was being “controlled from Adoor and from a particular house.” Referring to a flat in Panampilly Nagar and a vehicle bearing the registration number 20-20, he hinted that he possessed information about those involved but declined to disclose further details immediately. “Everything is in my diary, the teacher and the disciple will both be trapped,” he warned, adding that he should not be unnecessarily provoked. He warned that if forced to reveal everything, “the respectable public image of certain people will be torn apart.” Mr Unnithan said he had always been “a lone fighter” within the party and had stood with former Congress leader K Karunakaran and Oommen Chandy “without expecting positions or personal gains.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Responding to allegations concerning his family, Mr Unnithan asserted that his son had never joined the BJP. Taking an apparent dig at Padmaja Venugopal, he said it was “the children of those who had secured everything” within the Congress who had crossed over to the BJP.

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Intensifying the internal conflict within the Congress in Keralam, Kasaragod MP Rajmohan Unnithan on Tuesday launched a sharp attack on fellow party leader Shafi Parambil, MP, alleging that a coordinated cyber campaign was being orchestrated against him and warning that he would expose those behind it if the attacks continued. Challenging Mr. Parambil to an open public debate, Mr Unnithan said he was “ready to end his political career” if Mr Parambil could prove that his allegations were baseless. He also claimed that he had recorded all relevant details in his personal diary and warned that the people involved, whom he described as “the teacher and the disciple”, would eventually be exposed. Mr Unnithan dismissed the claim that Mr. Parambil belonged to the ‘A’ group in the Congress, saying it would be “the eighth wonder of the world” to describe him as an A group leader. He clarified that he had not insulted Mr Parambil but had only stated that he did not belong to the group. Taking aim at those invoking the legacy of the late former Chief Minister Oommen Chandy, Mr Unnithan said many Congress leaders had stayed away when Chandy was being targeted, while others were concerned about protecting the public image. He questioned where those now speaking about the “Oommen Chandy school of politics” had been at the time. He also maintained that he had not received any personal benefits in Chandy’s name. Mr Unnithan alleged that the social media attacks against him were being conducted through fake accounts as part of a deliberate campaign rather than being spontaneous criticism. He claimed that the operation was being “controlled from Adoor and from a particular house.” Referring to a flat in Panampilly Nagar and a vehicle bearing the registration number 20-20, he hinted that he possessed information about those involved but declined to disclose further details immediately. “Everything is in my diary, the teacher and the disciple will both be trapped,” he warned, adding that he should not be unnecessarily provoked. He warned that if forced to reveal everything, “the respectable public image of certain people will be torn apart.” Mr Unnithan said he had always been “a lone fighter” within the party and had stood with former Congress leader K Karunakaran and Oommen Chandy “without expecting positions or personal gains.”
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Responding to allegations concerning his family, Mr Unnithan asserted that his son had never joined the BJP. Taking an apparent dig at Padmaja Venugopal, he said it was “the children of those who had secured everything” within the Congress who had crossed over to the BJP.

articles.title: After six years apart, BJP and Akali Dal announce alliance for Punjab Assembly election
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Prime Minister Narendra Modi hails the move as ‘putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first’

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Six years after parting ways because of differences over the three farm laws, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and its oldest ally, the Shiromani Akali Dali (SAD ), reunited ahead of the Assembly election in Punjab, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi hailing the move as “putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first”. The announcement of the return of the SAD to the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) headed by the BJP was made at a press conference held at the BJP’s headquarters in New Delhi, and addressed by Union Home Minister Amit Shah, SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal, and BJP president Nitin Nabin. Seat adjustment details are yet to be ironed out, according to Mr. Nabin, who said talks in this regard were ongoing, while Mr. Shah clarified that the SAD would continue to hold the status of “elder brother” or the more dominant partner in the State, with a claim to the Chief Minister’s post if the alliance came to power. “It is usually the elder brother who has a claim to the CM’s post,” Mr. Shah said. The alliance’s goal was to make Punjab drug-free by December 31, 2029, and make sure that law and order, development, and issues pertaining to farmers were addressed, the Home Minister also said. Mr. Badal hailed the long history and personal equations between senior leaders of the BJP, the late former PM Atal Behari Vajpayee and L.K. Advani, with his own father, late CM of Punjab, Parkash Singh Badal, who had, between the three of them, fashioned the alliance in 1996. “This is not a political alliance; it’s an alliance of people’s sentiments,” Mr. Sukhbir Badal said, emphasising Hindu- Sikh unity and harmony, as did Mr. Nabin in his remarks. The PM would be attending a public meeting in Moga on December 8, Mr. Sukhbir Badal said, marking the birth anniversary of Parkash Singh Badal. VIDEO | Delhi: During a joint press conference, Union Home Minister Amit Shah (@AmitShah) says, "BJP, the Akali Dal, and the NDA will contest in Punjab, and we will announce several key points in our manifesto. But, I want to make one thing very clear: eliminating drugs from Punjab will be our primary goal, eliminating corruption in Punjab will be our primary goal, and strengthening nationalist forces in Punjab will also be our primary goal. The current government in the state, led by Kejriwal Ji, had come to power promising to eliminate drugs within three months. They promised to eliminate drugs, but the problem has not been eradicated; it has increased. In 2017, Rahul Gandhi Ji had promised that drugs would be eliminated within one term. He made that promise, but his party also did nothing to address the drug problem. Now, I want to reiterate a promise that I made there: by December 31, 2029, we will make Punjab completely drug-free." (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/bIyFWTfmBd) While the contours of the exact seat-sharing agreement are yet to be decided, in the past, the BJP contested 23 out of the 117 seats in the fray, a situation that is likely to change, with the BJP being given more seats, albeit still fewer than the SAD. The alliance had won 93 seats in the 1997 Assembly election, with the SAD winning 75 seats and the BJP winning 18 seats. After losing power to the Congress in 2002, the alliance returned to office in 2007 with 68 seats and retained power in 2012 with an identical tally, bucking Punjab’s trend of voting out incumbent governments.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The SAD walked away from the NDA in 2020, with party MP Harsimrat Badal also resigning her position as Minister in the Modi government at the Centre over the three farm laws that sought to re-engineer agri-commerce, igniting months-long protests on Delhi’s borders. To a question by the media on what the SAD had to say about the farm laws now, Mr. Shah answered that since the farm Bills had been withdrawn by the government, “there is no point in asking the question”.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 After six years apart, BJP and Akali Dal announce alliance for Punjab Assembly election

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 05:12:09 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Prime Minister Narendra Modi hails the move as ‘putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first’

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Six years after parting ways because of differences over the three farm laws, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and its oldest ally, the Shiromani Akali Dali (SAD ), reunited ahead of the Assembly election in Punjab, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi hailing the move as “putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first”. The announcement of the return of the SAD to the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) headed by the BJP was made at a press conference held at the BJP’s headquarters in New Delhi, and addressed by Union Home Minister Amit Shah, SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal, and BJP president Nitin Nabin. Seat adjustment details are yet to be ironed out, according to Mr. Nabin, who said talks in this regard were ongoing, while Mr. Shah clarified that the SAD would continue to hold the status of “elder brother” or the more dominant partner in the State, with a claim to the Chief Minister’s post if the alliance came to power. “It is usually the elder brother who has a claim to the CM’s post,” Mr. Shah said. The alliance’s goal was to make Punjab drug-free by December 31, 2029, and make sure that law and order, development, and issues pertaining to farmers were addressed, the Home Minister also said. Mr. Badal hailed the long history and personal equations between senior leaders of the BJP, the late former PM Atal Behari Vajpayee and L.K. Advani, with his own father, late CM of Punjab, Parkash Singh Badal, who had, between the three of them, fashioned the alliance in 1996. “This is not a political alliance; it’s an alliance of people’s sentiments,” Mr. Sukhbir Badal said, emphasising Hindu- Sikh unity and harmony, as did Mr. Nabin in his remarks. The PM would be attending a public meeting in Moga on December 8, Mr. Sukhbir Badal said, marking the birth anniversary of Parkash Singh Badal. VIDEO | Delhi: During a joint press conference, Union Home Minister Amit Shah (@AmitShah) says, "BJP, the Akali Dal, and the NDA will contest in Punjab, and we will announce several key points in our manifesto. But, I want to make one thing very clear: eliminating drugs from Punjab will be our primary goal, eliminating corruption in Punjab will be our primary goal, and strengthening nationalist forces in Punjab will also be our primary goal. The current government in the state, led by Kejriwal Ji, had come to power promising to eliminate drugs within three months. They promised to eliminate drugs, but the problem has not been eradicated; it has increased. In 2017, Rahul Gandhi Ji had promised that drugs would be eliminated within one term. He made that promise, but his party also did nothing to address the drug problem. Now, I want to reiterate a promise that I made there: by December 31, 2029, we will make Punjab completely drug-free." (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/bIyFWTfmBd) While the contours of the exact seat-sharing agreement are yet to be decided, in the past, the BJP contested 23 out of the 117 seats in the fray, a situation that is likely to change, with the BJP being given more seats, albeit still fewer than the SAD. The alliance had won 93 seats in the 1997 Assembly election, with the SAD winning 75 seats and the BJP winning 18 seats. After losing power to the Congress in 2002, the alliance returned to office in 2007 with 68 seats and retained power in 2012 with an identical tally, bucking Punjab’s trend of voting out incumbent governments.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The SAD walked away from the NDA in 2020, with party MP Harsimrat Badal also resigning her position as Minister in the Modi government at the Centre over the three farm laws that sought to re-engineer agri-commerce, igniting months-long protests on Delhi’s borders. To a question by the media on what the SAD had to say about the farm laws now, Mr. Shah answered that since the farm Bills had been withdrawn by the government, “there is no point in asking the question”.

🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "After six years apart, BJP and Akali Dal announce alliance for Punjab Assembly election", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Prime Minister Narendra Modi hails the move as ‘putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first’.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'After six years apart, BJP and Akali Dal announc' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'After six years apart, BJP and Akali Dal anno' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'After six years apart, BJP and Akali Dal anno' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Prime Minister Narendra Modi hails the move as ‘putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first’." (Hinglish Arth: प्रधान मंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने इस कदम को 'पंजाब और पंजाबियों के कल्याण को पहले स्थान पर रखने' वाला कदम बताया।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "After six years apart, BJP and Akali Dal announce alliance for Punjab Assembly election"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Shah answered that since the farm Bills had been withdrawn by the government, “there is no point in asking the question”.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Shah answered that since the farm Bills had been withdrawn by the government, “there is no point in asking the question”." (Hinglish Arth: शाह ने जवाब दिया कि चूंकि सरकार ने कृषि बिल वापस ले लिया है, इसलिए "सवाल पूछने का कोई मतलब नहीं है"।)

articles.title: Thirupparankundram 'deepathoon' row LIVE: Tamil Nadu BJP chief arrested, tight security in hillock on Karthigai Deepam day
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: All eyes are on Thirupparankundram on the day of Karthigai Deepam festival on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) following the Supreme Court's recent interim order allowing lighting of lamp on the controversial 'deepathoon' atop the hill in Madurai district.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Former Union Minister and BJP leader L. Murugan who was stopped by the police near the Annur bus stop in Coimbatore district, questioned the imposition of restrictions on his movement in Coimbatore district when the prohibitory orders were applicable to Madurai district. Speaking to reporters, Mr. Murugan said: “There is no relevance to the prohibitory orders imposed in Madurai to restrict movement in Coimbatore district. The police have not given me proper information or explained the reason for stopping me,” he said on Tuesday — T.C. Sibi Sreevathson Nainar Nagenthran, who left his home in Tirunelveli district at 2.35 pm for Thirupparankundram, was arrested at Thatchanallur check-post on Tirunelveli City outskirts at 3.15 pm along with a group of party functionaries. Police team led by Assistant Commissioner of Police, Palayamkottai, Rajamurali Ramachandran has been deployed in front of the house of Mr. Nagenthran to stop him from going to Thirupparankundram to participate in Karthigai Deepam festival. Here’s a look at the history and legal background of this long-running dispute. When a row broke out over lighting of Karthigai Deepam at the hill in Madurai, four Sthaneeka Bhattars of the Subramaniaswami Temple testified that the lamp had been lit at the Uchipillaiyar Temple since “time immemorial” The Bhattars conveyed this in a communication written to the temple authorities against the backdrop of a raging row over the Hindu Munnani’s demand for lighting the deepam at a different place. Explore the 30-year-old controversy over Karthigai Deepam lighting at Thirupparankundram, featuring testimonies from Sthaneeka Bhattars. In Thirupparankundram in Madurai, Hindus and Muslims live in camaraderie, but that has not kept the hill, which holds a couple of temples, a dargah, and some Jain beds, out of dispute. Here, we outline the history of judgments involving different petitioners through the years, in an attempt to understand the current crisis.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Explore the legal and political tensions in Thirupparankundram, where communal harmony faces challenges over religious practices and land disputes.

articles.title: Sonia Gandhi recalls ‘pull of power’ while deciding against becoming PM in 2004
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: She said it was a lesson about power that ‘once you have it, you may find excuses to keep it.’

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi has said she felt the "pull of power" while deciding on whether she should take up the prime ministership in 2004, as she thought that she owed it to party workers who had rallied across the country during the election campaign to accept the post. She said it was a lesson about power that "once you have it, you may find excuses to keep it". The observations came during a conversation with her son Rahul Gandhi and daughter Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, a video of which was shared by them on social media platforms. In the video shared days after the launch of Sonia Gandhi's memoir 'Belonging: A Journey Of Love' , the three are seen reminiscing about moments of joy, laughter and pain they felt at various points in time. In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi shared the video and said, "Ma's journey of Belonging has been full of enormous love and terrible tragedy, and she has met all of it with dignity and courage." The proposal didn't go according to plan and neither did my seventh birthday. The decision in 2004 gave some of us relief but others joy. There was an intention behind withdrawing Papa's security. And even after 500+ pages there are some things Ma has left out of her book. Priyanka and I sat down with our mother to talk through all of it. Going back to those memories brought back the joy, the laughter and even the pain we felt at the time. Ma's journey of Belonging has been full of enormous love and terrible tragedy, and she has met all of it with dignity and courage. In the video, Sonia Gandhi talks in detail about the internal conflict she faced while deciding whether to take up the Prime Minister's post after the Congress-led UPA's victory in the 2004 Lok Sabha elections. She asserts that she did not want power. Talking about the time, Rahul Gandhi says there was a situation unfolding and "we were witnessing the situation from the inside". "On the one hand there was mum saying maybe, maybe not. On the other side there were seven people. There is one gentleman over there who is the best possible PM," he recalls, referring to Manmohan Singh.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: "The interesting thing is there is only one man who can be PM because of his qualities, capabilities, and there are six-seven dreamers who cannot be. Then my mother decides - 'No (not taking up premiership)'; there is actually joy in the room," he says.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 Sonia Gandhi recalls ‘pull of power’ while deciding against becoming PM in 2004

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 05:10:10 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: She said it was a lesson about power that ‘once you have it, you may find excuses to keep it.’

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi has said she felt the "pull of power" while deciding on whether she should take up the prime ministership in 2004, as she thought that she owed it to party workers who had rallied across the country during the election campaign to accept the post. She said it was a lesson about power that "once you have it, you may find excuses to keep it". The observations came during a conversation with her son Rahul Gandhi and daughter Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, a video of which was shared by them on social media platforms. In the video shared days after the launch of Sonia Gandhi's memoir 'Belonging: A Journey Of Love' , the three are seen reminiscing about moments of joy, laughter and pain they felt at various points in time. In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi shared the video and said, "Ma's journey of Belonging has been full of enormous love and terrible tragedy, and she has met all of it with dignity and courage." The proposal didn't go according to plan and neither did my seventh birthday. The decision in 2004 gave some of us relief but others joy. There was an intention behind withdrawing Papa's security. And even after 500+ pages there are some things Ma has left out of her book. Priyanka and I sat down with our mother to talk through all of it. Going back to those memories brought back the joy, the laughter and even the pain we felt at the time. Ma's journey of Belonging has been full of enormous love and terrible tragedy, and she has met all of it with dignity and courage. In the video, Sonia Gandhi talks in detail about the internal conflict she faced while deciding whether to take up the Prime Minister's post after the Congress-led UPA's victory in the 2004 Lok Sabha elections. She asserts that she did not want power. Talking about the time, Rahul Gandhi says there was a situation unfolding and "we were witnessing the situation from the inside". "On the one hand there was mum saying maybe, maybe not. On the other side there were seven people. There is one gentleman over there who is the best possible PM," he recalls, referring to Manmohan Singh.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: "The interesting thing is there is only one man who can be PM because of his qualities, capabilities, and there are six-seven dreamers who cannot be. Then my mother decides - 'No (not taking up premiership)'; there is actually joy in the room," he says.

articles.title: Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Jensen Huang’s return

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Wall Street’s main indexes rallied sharply on Monday (November 23, 2026), led by a ​nearly 7% jump in the tech-heavy Nasdaq, as investors rushed back into AI-linked stocks ⁠after Nvidia said it had reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Mr. Huang’s return. Mr. Huang resigned ‌as chief executive earlier this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The chipmaker is widely regarded as a cornerstone of the AI trade, and ‌its sharp rebound helped lift sentiment across the sector after weeks of heavy selling. “Huang’s return ‌marks ⁠one of the biggest reversals in the history of the stock market. Never has so ⁠much value rested on the shoulders of a single executive,” said David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation. “Wall Street envisioned a stock market without his leadership and didn’t like what it saw.” The Nasdaq-100 was on track to add more than $2 trillion ​in market value on Monday (November 23). The Nasdaq ‌Composite and the S&P 500 were on track for their biggest one-day gains since markets surged after Mr. Trump paused his “Liberation Day” tariff package in April 2025. Chip stocks gained, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 13.4% and also on track for its best session since April 2025.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The rally was broad-based in ‌the tech sphere, with the so-called Magnificent Seven stocks Tesla, Amazon , Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet climbing ​between 5.8% and 12.4%.

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #18 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 12:26:40 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Jensen Huang’s return

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Wall Street’s main indexes rallied sharply on Monday (November 23, 2026), led by a ​nearly 7% jump in the tech-heavy Nasdaq, as investors rushed back into AI-linked stocks ⁠after Nvidia said it had reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Mr. Huang’s return. Mr. Huang resigned ‌as chief executive earlier this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The chipmaker is widely regarded as a cornerstone of the AI trade, and ‌its sharp rebound helped lift sentiment across the sector after weeks of heavy selling. “Huang’s return ‌marks ⁠one of the biggest reversals in the history of the stock market. Never has so ⁠much value rested on the shoulders of a single executive,” said David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation. “Wall Street envisioned a stock market without his leadership and didn’t like what it saw.” The Nasdaq-100 was on track to add more than $2 trillion ​in market value on Monday (November 23). The Nasdaq ‌Composite and the S&P 500 were on track for their biggest one-day gains since markets surged after Mr. Trump paused his “Liberation Day” tariff package in April 2025. Chip stocks gained, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 13.4% and also on track for its best session since April 2025.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The rally was broad-based in ‌the tech sphere, with the so-called Magnificent Seven stocks Tesla, Amazon , Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet climbing ​between 5.8% and 12.4%.

Extramarital (Adjective)
शादी के पहला — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Extramarital' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Liberation (Noun)
मुक्ति — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Liberation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Executive (Adjective)
कार्यकारिणी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Executive' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 📈 Economic, Banking & Finance passage on "Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jens' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates J' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates J' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed..." (Hinglish Arth: एनवीडिया के शेयरों में 32.2% की वृद्धि हुई, जो एक असाधारण उलटफेर के बाद दो दशकों से अधिक समय में अपनी सबसे बड़ी एक दिवसीय छलांग की राह पर है, जिसके बाद जेन्सेन हुआंग की वापसी के लिए राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रम्प का आह्वान हुआ।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The rally was broad-based in ‌the tech sphere, with the so-called Magnificent Seven stocks Tesla, Amazon , Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet climbing...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The rally was broad-based in ‌the tech sphere, with the so-called Magnificent Seven stocks Tesla, Amazon , Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet climbing..." articles.title: Sri Lanka’s Opposition lawmakers accuse government of preventing parliamentary debate on Imran Khan’s release
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Cannot entertain motion that could impact bilateral ties, said the Sri Lanka government

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Opposition lawmakers in Sri Lanka have accused the government of preventing a parliamentary debate on the release of jailed former Prime Minister of Pakistan Imran Khan. Last week, the state-run Daily News reported that the Sri Lankan Parliament was scheduled to hold an adjournment debate on November 21, 2026, on a motion moved by Opposition MP Ajith P. Perera, from the main Opposition party Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB or United People’s Power), calling for Mr. Khan’s release on humanitarian grounds. The debate did not take place. Mr. Perera expressed disappointment and said it was “regrettable that the motion has been rejected even before being debated.” Defending the government’s position, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Arun Hemachandra said the government did not wish to entertain matters that could create “diplomatic tensions” or affect ties with Sri Lanka’s bilateral partners. However, Mr. Hemachandra observed that Mr. Perera was free to express his personal views on the matter during the time allocated to him in Parliament. Addressing Parliament on Monday (November 23, 2026), SJB MP and Leader of the Sri Lanka Muslim Congress Rauff Hakeem attacked the government for pursuing a “transactional” foreign policy, rather than one based on principles. Pakistan, he said, had been “a longstanding friend” of Sri Lanka, supporting the island during difficult times. He recalled Pakistan’s assistance during the pandemic and Mr. Khan’s crucial intervention in urging the Gotabaya Rajapaksa government to end its mandatory cremations policy during the pandemic that had caused enormous distress among the island’s Muslim community. Sri Lanka and Pakistan have historically maintained close bilateral ties, regardless of the party in power in either country. Mr. Khan visited Colombo in February 2021, when he was Prime Minister. Gotabaya Rajapaksa was President of Sri Lanka at the time. Mr. Khan’s two-day visit was received very well by the local media as well as cricketing fans on the island, known for its passion for the game.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Further, Mr. Hakeem slammed the government’s position on the Palestine issue, contending that statements of support at international fora meant little without substantive domestic action. Sri Lanka’s ruling Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna [JVP or People’s Liberation Front] has historically supported the Palestinian cause. After its ascent to power in 2024, the National People’s Power coalition that the JVP leads has maintained ties with Israel and has continued to send Sri Lankan workers to Israel. In an interview to The Hindu in May 2026, Deputy Minister Mr. Hemachandra said: “We separated our Free Palestine stand and our diplomatic relationship with Israel as two different things. I think any country should have that choice. And when we take the opportunity to send workers to Israel, that does not change our stand on Palestine.”

hinglishTracks.en: Cannot entertain motion that could impact bilateral ties, said the Sri Lanka government

hinglishTracks.en: Opposition lawmakers in Sri Lanka have accused the government of preventing a parliamentary debate on the release of jailed former Prime Minister of Pakistan Imran Khan.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — श्रीलंका में विपक्षी सांसदों ने सरकार पर जेल में बंद पाकिस्तान के पूर्व प्रधानमंत्री इमरान खान की रिहाई पर संसदीय बहस को रोकने का आरोप लगाया है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Last week, the state-run Daily News reported that the Sri Lankan Parliament was scheduled to hold an adjournment debate on November 21, 2026, on a motion moved by Opposition MP Ajith P.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — पिछले हफ्ते, राज्य संचालित डेली न्यूज ने बताया कि श्रीलंकाई संसद विपक्षी सांसद अजित पी द्वारा पेश किए गए प्रस्ताव पर 21 नवंबर, 2026 को स्थगन बहस आयोजित करने वाली थी।।

hinglishTracks.en: Perera, from the main Opposition party Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB or United People’s Power), calling for Mr.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — मुख्य विपक्षी दल समागी जन बालवेगया (एसजेबी या यूनाइटेड पीपुल्स पावर) से परेरा ने श्रीमान की मांग की।।

hinglishTracks.en: Khan’s release on humanitarian grounds.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — मानवीय आधार पर खान की रिहाई.।

hinglishTracks.en: The debate did not take place.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — बहस नहीं हुई.।

hinglishTracks.en: Perera expressed disappointment and said it was “regrettable that the motion has been rejected even before being debated.”
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — परेरा ने निराशा व्यक्त की और कहा कि यह "अफसोसजनक है कि प्रस्ताव पर बहस होने से पहले ही खारिज कर दिया गया है।"। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Disappointment' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Disappointment' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: Defending the government’s position, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Arun Hemachandra said the government did not wish to entertain matters that could create “diplomatic tensions” or affect ties with Sri Lanka’s bilateral partners.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — सरकार की स्थिति का बचाव करते हुए, विदेश मामलों के उप मंत्री अरुण हेमचंद्र ने कहा कि सरकार उन मामलों पर विचार नहीं करना चाहती जो "राजनयिक तनाव" पैदा कर सकते हैं या श्रीलंका के द्विपक्षीय भागीदारों के साथ संबंधों को प्रभावित कर सकते हैं।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Bilateral' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: द्विपक्षीय — दो देशों के बीच आपसी समझौता, व्यापार या कूटनीतिक बातचीत। इसके Synonyms हैं: Reciprocal, Two-sided, Mutual और Antonyms हैं: Unilateral, Multilateral, One-way।

hinglishTracks.en: Hemachandra observed that Mr.

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — परेरा संसद में आवंटित समय के दौरान इस मामले पर अपने व्यक्तिगत विचार व्यक्त करने के लिए स्वतंत्र थे।।

hinglishTracks.en: Addressing Parliament on Monday (November 23, 2026), SJB MP and Leader of the Sri Lanka Muslim Congress Rauff Hakeem attacked the government for pursuing a “transactional” foreign policy, rather than one based on principles.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — सोमवार (नवंबर 23, 2026) को संसद को संबोधित करते हुए, एसजेबी सांसद और श्रीलंका मुस्लिम कांग्रेस के नेता रउफ हकीम ने सिद्धांतों पर आधारित विदेश नीति के बजाय "लेन-देन" वाली विदेश नीति अपनाने के लिए सरकार पर हमला किया।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Transactional' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Transactional' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #19 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 Sri Lanka’s Opposition lawmakers accuse government of preventing parliamentary debate on Imran Khan’s release

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 05:09:21 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Cannot entertain motion that could impact bilateral ties, said the Sri Lanka government

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Opposition lawmakers in Sri Lanka have accused the government of preventing a parliamentary debate on the release of jailed former Prime Minister of Pakistan Imran Khan. Last week, the state-run Daily News reported that the Sri Lankan Parliament was scheduled to hold an adjournment debate on November 21, 2026, on a motion moved by Opposition MP Ajith P. Perera, from the main Opposition party Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB or United People’s Power), calling for Mr. Khan’s release on humanitarian grounds. The debate did not take place. Mr. Perera expressed disappointment and said it was “regrettable that the motion has been rejected even before being debated.” Defending the government’s position, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Arun Hemachandra said the government did not wish to entertain matters that could create “diplomatic tensions” or affect ties with Sri Lanka’s bilateral partners. However, Mr. Hemachandra observed that Mr. Perera was free to express his personal views on the matter during the time allocated to him in Parliament. Addressing Parliament on Monday (November 23, 2026), SJB MP and Leader of the Sri Lanka Muslim Congress Rauff Hakeem attacked the government for pursuing a “transactional” foreign policy, rather than one based on principles. Pakistan, he said, had been “a longstanding friend” of Sri Lanka, supporting the island during difficult times. He recalled Pakistan’s assistance during the pandemic and Mr. Khan’s crucial intervention in urging the Gotabaya Rajapaksa government to end its mandatory cremations policy during the pandemic that had caused enormous distress among the island’s Muslim community. Sri Lanka and Pakistan have historically maintained close bilateral ties, regardless of the party in power in either country. Mr. Khan visited Colombo in February 2021, when he was Prime Minister. Gotabaya Rajapaksa was President of Sri Lanka at the time. Mr. Khan’s two-day visit was received very well by the local media as well as cricketing fans on the island, known for its passion for the game.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Further, Mr. Hakeem slammed the government’s position on the Palestine issue, contending that statements of support at international fora meant little without substantive domestic action. Sri Lanka’s ruling Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna [JVP or People’s Liberation Front] has historically supported the Palestinian cause. After its ascent to power in 2024, the National People’s Power coalition that the JVP leads has maintained ties with Israel and has continued to send Sri Lankan workers to Israel. In an interview to The Hindu in May 2026, Deputy Minister Mr. Hemachandra said: “We separated our Free Palestine stand and our diplomatic relationship with Israel as two different things. I think any country should have that choice. And when we take the opportunity to send workers to Israel, that does not change our stand on Palestine.”

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Cannot entertain motion that could impact bilateral ties, said the Sri Lanka government
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Opposition lawmakers in Sri Lanka have accused the government of preventing a parliamentary debate on the release of jailed former Prime Minister of Pakistan Imran Khan. Last week, the state-run Daily News reported that the Sri Lankan Parliament was scheduled to hold an adjournment debate on November 21, 2026, on a motion moved by Opposition MP Ajith P. Perera, from the main Opposition party Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB or United People’s Power), calling for Mr. Khan’s release on humanitarian grounds. The debate did not take place. Mr. Perera expressed disappointment and said it was “regrettable that the motion has been rejected even before being debated.” Defending the government’s position, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Arun Hemachandra said the government did not wish to entertain matters that could create “diplomatic tensions” or affect ties with Sri Lanka’s bilateral partners. However, Mr. Hemachandra observed that Mr. Perera was free to express his personal views on the matter during the time allocated to him in Parliament. Addressing Parliament on Monday (November 23, 2026), SJB MP and Leader of the Sri Lanka Muslim Congress Rauff Hakeem attacked the government for pursuing a “transactional” foreign policy, rather than one based on principles. Pakistan, he said, had been “a longstanding friend” of Sri Lanka, supporting the island during difficult times. He recalled Pakistan’s assistance during the pandemic and Mr. Khan’s crucial intervention in urging the Gotabaya Rajapaksa government to end its mandatory cremations policy during the pandemic that had caused enormous distress among the island’s Muslim community. Sri Lanka and Pakistan have historically maintained close bilateral ties, regardless of the party in power in either country. Mr. Khan visited Colombo in February 2021, when he was Prime Minister. Gotabaya Rajapaksa was President of Sri Lanka at the time. Mr. Khan’s two-day visit was received very well by the local media as well as cricketing fans on the island, known for its passion for the game.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Further, Mr. Hakeem slammed the government’s position on the Palestine issue, contending that statements of support at international fora meant little without substantive domestic action. Sri Lanka’s ruling Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna [JVP or People’s Liberation Front] has historically supported the Palestinian cause. After its ascent to power in 2024, the National People’s Power coalition that the JVP leads has maintained ties with Israel and has continued to send Sri Lankan workers to Israel. In an interview to The Hindu in May 2026, Deputy Minister Mr. Hemachandra said: “We separated our Free Palestine stand and our diplomatic relationship with Israel as two different things. I think any country should have that choice. And when we take the opportunity to send workers to Israel, that does not change our stand on Palestine.”

articles.title: Sheikh Hasina could only be brought back to Bangladesh in handcuffs: Humaiun Kobir
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: “She can only be brought back in handcuffs or under strict surveillance,” Bangladesh State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina could only be brought back to Bangladesh in handcuffs or under strict surveillance, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), according to a local media report. Ms. Hasina, 79, has been living in India since fleeing Bangladesh on August 5, 2024, following a student-led protest that toppled her government. Bangladesh has been seeking her extradition from India, while New Delhi has maintained that Dhaka's extradition request was being examined through a legal process. Ms. Hasina’s spokesman Syed Mozammel Ali, speaking to a news agency on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), said she would return on December 16, which Bangladesh celebrates as Victory Day to commemorate independence from Pakistan after the 1971 war. Ms. Hasina has urged Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to arrange her return on the national airline. “Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5th, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka,” the spokesman said. Responding to the news report, Mr. Kobir said, “She can only be brought back in handcuffs or under strict surveillance." "A distinction had to be drawn between what Hasina wanted and what could happen," he was quoted as saying by the state-run BSS news agency. The issue of Ms. Hasina's return has emerged as a major source of tension between Dhaka and New Delhi, with the latest wave of unrest in Bangladesh following the government's rejection of her request for a fresh passport and national identity card earlier this month.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ms. Hasina's lawyers had approached the Bangladesh mission in New Delhi seeking the documents to facilitate her planned return in December.

1. Core Context & Background: “She can only be brought back in handcuffs or under strict surveillance,” Bangladesh State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina could only be brought back to Bangladesh in handcuffs or under strict surveillance, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), according to a local media report. Ms. Hasina, 79, has been living in India since fleeing Bangladesh on August 5, 2024, following a student-led protest that toppled her government. Bangladesh has been seeking her extradition from India, while New Delhi has maintained that Dhaka's extradition request was being examined through a legal process. Ms. Hasina’s spokesman Syed Mozammel Ali, speaking to a news agency on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), said she would return on December 16, which Bangladesh celebrates as Victory Day to commemorate independence from Pakistan after the 1971 war. Responding to the news report, Mr. Kobir said, “She can only be brought back in handcuffs or under strict surveillance." "A distinction had to be drawn between what Hasina wanted and what could happen," he was quoted as saying by the state-run BSS news agency. The issue of Ms. Hasina's return has emerged as a major source of tension between Dhaka and New Delhi, with the latest wave of unrest in Bangladesh following the government's rejection of her request for a fresh passport and national identity card earlier this month.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: “She can only be brought back in handcuffs or under strict surveillance,” Bangladesh State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina could only be brought back to Bangladesh in handcuffs or under strict surveillance, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), according to a local media report. Ms. Hasina, 79, has been living in India since fleeing Bangladesh on August 5, 2024, following a student-led protest that toppled her government. Bangladesh has been seeking her extradition from India, while New Delhi has maintained that Dhaka's extradition request was being examined through a legal process. Ms. Hasina’s spokesman Syed Mozammel Ali, speaking to a news agency on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), said she would return on December 16, which Bangladesh celebrates as Victory Day to commemorate independence from Pakistan after the 1971 war. Ms. Hasina has urged Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to arrange her return on the national airline. “Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5th, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka,” the spokesman said. Responding to the news report, Mr. Kobir said, “She can only be brought back in handcuffs or under strict surveillance." "A distinction had to be drawn between what Hasina wanted and what could happen," he was quoted as saying by the state-run BSS news agency. The issue of Ms. Hasina's return has emerged as a major source of tension between Dhaka and New Delhi, with the latest wave of unrest in Bangladesh following the government's rejection of her request for a fresh passport and national identity card earlier this month.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ms. Hasina's lawyers had approached the Bangladesh mission in New Delhi seeking the documents to facilitate her planned return in December.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Ms. Hasina went into exile in India on August 5, 2024, after a student-led mass uprising forced her to end her 15-year rule

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans to return home from exile in India on December 16, the day the country celebrates as Victory Day when it won independence after a war with Pakistan. Ms. Hasina went into exile in India on August 5, 2024, after a student-led mass uprising forced her to end her 15-year rule. She was sentenced to death in absentia for crimes against humanity involving the uprising in which hundreds of protesters were killed. Ms. Hasina rejected the verdict and has said she is ready fight the case once she is back. In the statement on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) announcing the planned date of her return, she urged current Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to arrange her return on the national airline. “Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5th, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka,” spokesman Syed Mozammel Ali said in the statement. “It is deeply symbolic that she has chosen 16 December, our Victory Day, for her planned return to Bangladesh. We firmly believe that she will celebrate this historic day among her people, honoring the great victory achieved under the leadership of her father, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman,” Abu Obaidha Arin, an aide to Ms. Hasina, told The Associated Press . “We are equally confident that, she will definitely return and under her leadership post return, Bangladesh will once again advance towards peace, stability and prosperity,” Mr. Arin said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Earlier this month, in an interview with The Associated Press , Ms. Hasina said she would return to the country in December at any cost, and even death could not prevent her from returning home.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #23 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 Sheikh Hasina plans to return to Bangladesh from exile on December 16, spokesperson says

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 03:13:38 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Ms. Hasina went into exile in India on August 5, 2024, after a student-led mass uprising forced her to end her 15-year rule

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans to return home from exile in India on December 16, the day the country celebrates as Victory Day when it won independence after a war with Pakistan. Ms. Hasina went into exile in India on August 5, 2024, after a student-led mass uprising forced her to end her 15-year rule. She was sentenced to death in absentia for crimes against humanity involving the uprising in which hundreds of protesters were killed. Ms. Hasina rejected the verdict and has said she is ready fight the case once she is back. In the statement on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) announcing the planned date of her return, she urged current Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to arrange her return on the national airline. “Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5th, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka,” spokesman Syed Mozammel Ali said in the statement. “It is deeply symbolic that she has chosen 16 December, our Victory Day, for her planned return to Bangladesh. We firmly believe that she will celebrate this historic day among her people, honoring the great victory achieved under the leadership of her father, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman,” Abu Obaidha Arin, an aide to Ms. Hasina, told The Associated Press . “We are equally confident that, she will definitely return and under her leadership post return, Bangladesh will once again advance towards peace, stability and prosperity,” Mr. Arin said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Earlier this month, in an interview with The Associated Press , Ms. Hasina said she would return to the country in December at any cost, and even death could not prevent her from returning home.

Independence (Adjective / Verb)

✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Statement' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🌐 International & Geopolitics passage on "Sheikh Hasina plans to return to Bangladesh from exile on December 16, spokesperson says", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Hasina went into exile in India on August 5, 2024, after a student-led mass uprising forced her to end her 15-year rule.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Sheikh Hasina plans to return to Bangladesh from' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Sheikh Hasina plans to return to Bangladesh f' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Sheikh Hasina plans to return to Bangladesh f' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Hasina went into exile in India on August 5, 2024, after a student-led mass uprising forced her to end her 15-year rule." (Hinglish Arth: 5 अगस्त, 2024 को हसीना भारत में निर्वासन में चली गईं, जब एक छात्र के नेतृत्व वाले जन विद्रोह ने उन्हें अपने 15 साल के शासन को समाप्त करने के लिए मजबूर किया।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Sheikh Hasina plans to return to Bangladesh from exile on December 16, spokesperson says"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Hasina said she would return to the country in December at any cost, and even death could not prevent her from returning home.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Hasina said she would return to the country in December at any cost, and even death could not prevent her from returning home." (Hinglish Arth: हसीना ने कहा कि वह दिसंबर में किसी भी कीमत पर देश लौटेंगी और मौत भी उन्हें घर लौटने से नहीं रोक सकती।)

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The protests in the Afghan city in the first week of June were triggered by the enforcement of a dress code, which requires women to wear burqa in public; many women, including those wearing traditional Afghan wear of manto, were arrested, but released later as entire communities protested

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The chants were familiar. But this time, they echoed not in Tehran, but in Herat. In mid-June, Afghanistan’s western city of Herat witnessed a rare display of public defiance against the Taliban. Women, and this time, men too, marched through the streets chanting “Women, Work and Freedom”, a slogan probably inspired by Iran’s 2022 “Woman, Life and Freedom” movement that emerged after the death of the 22-year-old Mahsa Amini. According to Zan Times , an exiled media organisation run by Afghan women journalists, the latest crackdown appears to have been planned days in advance. On June 4, Herat’s governor Noor Ahmad Islamjar reportedly met with a group of morality enforcers. On the afternoon of June 5, Taliban officials used the end of Friday prayers to announce that women who failed to comply with the Islamic dress code would be arrested. The following morning, the arrests began.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: World / Afghanistan / news media / demonstration / civil unrest / arrest / police / law enforcement / crime, law and justice

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — जून के पहले सप्ताह में अफगान शहर में विरोध प्रदर्शन एक ड्रेस कोड के लागू होने से शुरू हुआ था, जिसके तहत महिलाओं को सार्वजनिक रूप से बुर्का पहनने की आवश्यकता होती है; पारंपरिक अफ़ग़ान पोशाक मंटो पहनने वाली महिलाओं सहित कई महिलाओं को गिरफ़्तार किया गया, लेकिन बाद में पूरे समुदाय के विरोध के कारण उन्हें रिहा कर दिया गया। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Enforcement' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: सख्ती से कानून लागू करना — किसी नियम या आदेश का ज़मीनी स्तर पर पालन करवाना। इसके Synonyms हैं: Implementation, Execution, Administration और Antonyms हैं: Neglect, Abandonment, Waiver।

hinglishTracks.en: The chants were familiar.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — मंत्र परिचित थे.।

hinglishTracks.en: But this time, they echoed not in Tehran, but in Herat.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — लेकिन इस बार उनकी गूंज तेहरान में नहीं, बल्कि हेरात में सुनाई दी.।

📰 How Herat defied the Taliban regime, chanting ‘women, work and freedom’

Core Context & Background: The protests in the Afghan city in the first week of June were triggered by the enforcement of a dress code, which requires women to wear burqa in public; many women, including those wearing traditional Afghan wear of manto, were arrested, but released later as entire communities protested

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The chants were familiar. But this time, they echoed not in Tehran, but in Herat. In mid-June, Afghanistan’s western city of Herat witnessed a rare display of public defiance against the Taliban. Women, and this time, men too, marched through the streets chanting “Women, Work and Freedom”, a slogan probably inspired by Iran’s 2022 “Woman, Life and Freedom” movement that emerged after the death of the 22-year-old Mahsa Amini. According to Zan Times , an exiled media organisation run by Afghan women journalists, the latest crackdown appears to have been planned days in advance. On June 4, Herat’s governor Noor Ahmad Islamjar reportedly met with a group of morality enforcers. On the afternoon of June 5, Taliban officials used the end of Friday prayers to announce that women who failed to comply with the Islamic dress code would be arrested. The following morning, the arrests began.

articles.title: What do lemurs and opera singers share?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Recently, a study showed how indri lemurs use the same method opera singers use to ensure their vocals reach the audience at the back. In conversation with one of the researchers, Dr Chiara De Gregorio from the University of Warwick

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Have you seen opera performers sing? You might notice how their mouths move according to how high their pitch needs to be. Imagine finding out a primate in the rainforests of Madagascar has been doing the same, possibly even before opera began? With a pointy snout, large eyes and usually a long tail, you might have encountered this primate in one of your favourite movies, Madagascar. Remember King Julien, who loved to sing and dance? He was a type of lemur! So were Maurice and Mort, the two characters always around him. Endemic (naturally found only in) to the island of Madagascar, lemurs are primates with diverse activity patterns, and even though they share a resemblance with other primates, they evolved independently from monkeys, apes, etc. They are considered to be the world’s most endangered mammals by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN). This is mostly due to habitat loss, hunting and even unstable conservation efforts due to political and financial instabilities. While most lemurs might survive in captivity, there are specific species like the indri which can only survive in their natural habitat, making it extremely important for us to protect the forests and their home. Today, let’s talk about this very species — the indri or babakoto! One of the larger lemur species, the indri is the only singing lemur in the world. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement One of the larger lemur species, the indri is the only singing lemur in the world. These black-and-white-coated primates are known for their loud, often complex, and haunting territorial songs. They often sing as duets or group choruses and even use opera-like vocal techniques to reach higher pitches. This was, in fact, a quite recent discovery. Researchers from the University of Warwick and the University of Turin found that the world’s only singing lemur opens its mouth wider on higher notes, just like a trained soprano. The new study, published in PLOS Computational Biology , shows the first direct evidence that wild indris coordinate their mouth opening with the frequency of their songs. The research team analysed 83 video recordings of 19 wild indris, combining field audio with markerless motion-tracking technology. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement “The opera singers back in the day, before mics became a thing, used to tweak the shape of their mouth to sing louder and to reach farther to the audience sitting at the back. Imagine finding the same technique being used in the middle of a rainforest in Madagascar,” laughed Dr Chiara De Gregorio, corresponding author and Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Warwick.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Human singers are trained to widen their mouths as pitch rises, aligning the resonant frequencies of the vocal tract with the harmonics of the voice and amplifying the sound. For an animal communicating through a thick forest, it could make the difference between a song that carries and one that doesn’t.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #27 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 What do lemurs and opera singers share?

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 05:46:37 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Recently, a study showed how indri lemurs use the same method opera singers use to ensure their vocals reach the audience at the back. In conversation with one of the researchers, Dr Chiara De Gregorio from the University of Warwick

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Have you seen opera performers sing? You might notice how their mouths move according to how high their pitch needs to be. Imagine finding out a primate in the rainforests of Madagascar has been doing the same, possibly even before opera began? With a pointy snout, large eyes and usually a long tail, you might have encountered this primate in one of your favourite movies, Madagascar. Remember King Julien, who loved to sing and dance? He was a type of lemur! So were Maurice and Mort, the two characters always around him. Endemic (naturally found only in) to the island of Madagascar, lemurs are primates with diverse activity patterns, and even though they share a resemblance with other primates, they evolved independently from monkeys, apes, etc. They are considered to be the world’s most endangered mammals by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN). This is mostly due to habitat loss, hunting and even unstable conservation efforts due to political and financial instabilities. While most lemurs might survive in captivity, there are specific species like the indri which can only survive in their natural habitat, making it extremely important for us to protect the forests and their home. Today, let’s talk about this very species — the indri or babakoto! One of the larger lemur species, the indri is the only singing lemur in the world. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement One of the larger lemur species, the indri is the only singing lemur in the world. These black-and-white-coated primates are known for their loud, often complex, and haunting territorial songs. They often sing as duets or group choruses and even use opera-like vocal techniques to reach higher pitches. This was, in fact, a quite recent discovery. Researchers from the University of Warwick and the University of Turin found that the world’s only singing lemur opens its mouth wider on higher notes, just like a trained soprano. The new study, published in PLOS Computational Biology , shows the first direct evidence that wild indris coordinate their mouth opening with the frequency of their songs. The research team analysed 83 video recordings of 19 wild indris, combining field audio with markerless motion-tracking technology. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement “The opera singers back in the day, before mics became a thing, used to tweak the shape of their mouth to sing louder and to reach farther to the audience sitting at the back. Imagine finding the same technique being used in the middle of a rainforest in Madagascar,” laughed Dr Chiara De Gregorio, corresponding author and Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Warwick.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Human singers are trained to widen their mouths as pitch rises, aligning the resonant frequencies of the vocal tract with the harmonics of the voice and amplifying the sound. For an animal communicating through a thick forest, it could make the difference between a song that carries and one that doesn’t.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'International' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

कम्प्यूटेशनल — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Computational' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Conversation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Conversation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Conservation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Conservation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "What do lemurs and opera singers share?", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Recently, a study showed how indri lemurs use the same method opera singers use to ensure their vocals reach the audience at the back.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'What do lemurs and opera singers share?' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'What do lemurs and opera singers share?' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'What do lemurs and opera singers share?' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Recently, a study showed how indri lemurs use the same method opera singers use to ensure their vocals reach the audience at the back." (Hinglish Arth: हाल ही में, एक अध्ययन से पता चला है कि इंद्री लेमर्स उसी पद्धति का उपयोग करते हैं जो ओपेरा गायक यह सुनिश्चित करने के लिए करते हैं कि उनकी आवाज़ पीछे बैठे दर्शकों तक पहुंचे।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "What do lemurs and opera singers share?"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. For an animal communicating through a thick forest, it could make the difference between a song that carries and one that doesn’t.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "For an animal communicating through a thick forest, it could make the difference between a song that carries and one that doesn’t." (Hinglish Arth: घने जंगल में संचार करने वाले एक जानवर के लिए, यह उस गीत के बीच अंतर कर सकता है जो प्रसारित होता है और जो नहीं करता है।)

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The webinar will examine how autoimmune conditions develop, their common symptoms, the challenges in diagnosis, and current approaches to treatment and long-term management

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Hindu will conduct a free health webinar on Saturday, November 28, 2026, on the topic ‘Understanding Autoimmune Conditions’. The webinar will be held from 11.30 a.m. to 12.30 p.m. Autoimmune conditions occur when the immune system mistakenly attacks the body’s own tissues and organs. These disorders can affect different parts of the body, including the joints, skin, nervous system and other organs, and may present with a wide range of symptoms. The session will explore how autoimmune conditions develop, the role of the immune system, and the common signs and symptoms associated with these disorders. It will also discuss early warning signs, including persistent fatigue, joint pain, muscle weakness and neurological symptoms, and explain when these warrant medical attention. The discussion will examine the challenges involved in diagnosing autoimmune conditions, the role of clinical evaluation and diagnostic tests, and the treatment options available. The panellists will also discuss long-term disease management, monitoring, and the importance of timely diagnosis and appropriate treatment. Expert panellists include Aishwarya G., Consultant Rheumatologist and Clinical Immunologist, Apollo Speciality Hospitals, Chennai. She will discuss the immune mechanisms underlying autoimmune conditions, common rheumatological disorders, their symptoms, diagnostic approaches and current treatment options. The panel will also feature Prabash Prabhakaran, Director and Senior Consultant – Neurology, SIMS Hospital, Vadapalani, Chennai. He will discuss autoimmune conditions affecting the nervous system, the neurological symptoms they can cause, approaches to diagnosis and treatment, and the importance of recognising neurological manifestations. The session will be moderated by Zubeda Hamid, Senior Assistant Editor, The Hindu .
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: To register, click here or scan the QR code given below.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: The webinar will examine how autoimmune conditions develop, their common symptoms, the challenges in diagnosis, and current approaches to treatment and long-term management
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Hindu will conduct a free health webinar on Saturday, November 28, 2026, on the topic ‘Understanding Autoimmune Conditions’. The webinar will be held from 11.30 a.m. to 12.30 p.m. Autoimmune conditions occur when the immune system mistakenly attacks the body’s own tissues and organs. These disorders can affect different parts of the body, including the joints, skin, nervous system and other organs, and may present with a wide range of symptoms. The session will explore how autoimmune conditions develop, the role of the immune system, and the common signs and symptoms associated with these disorders. It will also discuss early warning signs, including persistent fatigue, joint pain, muscle weakness and neurological symptoms, and explain when these warrant medical attention. The discussion will examine the challenges involved in diagnosing autoimmune conditions, the role of clinical evaluation and diagnostic tests, and the treatment options available. The panellists will also discuss long-term disease management, monitoring, and the importance of timely diagnosis and appropriate treatment. Expert panellists include Aishwarya G., Consultant Rheumatologist and Clinical Immunologist, Apollo Speciality Hospitals, Chennai. She will discuss the immune mechanisms underlying autoimmune conditions, common rheumatological disorders, their symptoms, diagnostic approaches and current treatment options. The panel will also feature Prabash Prabhakaran, Director and Senior Consultant – Neurology, SIMS Hospital, Vadapalani, Chennai. He will discuss autoimmune conditions affecting the nervous system, the neurological symptoms they can cause, approaches to diagnosis and treatment, and the importance of recognising neurological manifestations. The session will be moderated by Zubeda Hamid, Senior Assistant Editor, The Hindu .
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: To register, click here or scan the QR code given below.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: In August, for the first time, Namma Metro had successfully facilitated the transportation of an organ

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: After a successful organ transport in August for the first time, Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) has once again facilitated the movement of a human organ. On September 11, a live human heart arranged by Sparsh Hospital was transported via Namma Metro from Yeshwanthpur station to South End Circle station en route to Apollo Hospital. According to BMRCL, the transport operation commenced at 11.01 p.m. and concluded at 11.21 p.m. covering seven stations in just 20 minutes. The BMRCL stated that the heart was carried inside Train ID 12, Train Set 29, accompanied by the hospital’s medical team. To ensure smooth movement, the Assistant Security Officer coordinated with the Sparsh team and metro security personnel, making special arrangements to avoid delays and provide a safe corridor for the critical transfer. Bengaluru Metro facilitates transportation of donor heart from Goraguntepalya to Bommasandra A live human heart arranged by Sparsh Hospital was transported via Namma Metro from Yeshwanthpur station to South End Circle station en route to Apollo Hospital on September 11, 2025. The organ was accompanied by the hospital’s medical team. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement In August, for the first time, Namma Metro had successfully facilitated the transportation of an organ. A donated human liver, meant for transplantation, was transported from Vydehi Hospital at Whitefield to Sparsh Hospital at R.R. Nagar. The operation was executed using a combination of ambulance and metro, significantly reducing travel time during peak traffic hours. After its first organ transport in August, #Bengaluru 's Namma Metro again facilitated an organ transport on Sept 11. A live human heart was moved from Yeshwanthpur to South End Circle in just 20 minutes for a transplant at Apollo Hospital. @the_hindu @THBengaluru pic.twitter.com/g3ZrWNMZ7M
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Bengaluru / public transport / health / medical service
