🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #30 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 Bengaluru metro facilitates organ transport for second time

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 04:16:45 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: In August, for the first time, Namma Metro had successfully facilitated the transportation of an organ

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: After a successful organ transport in August for the first time, Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) has once again facilitated the movement of a human organ. On September 11, a live human heart arranged by Sparsh Hospital was transported via Namma Metro from Yeshwanthpur station to South End Circle station en route to Apollo Hospital. According to BMRCL, the transport operation commenced at 11.01 p.m. and concluded at 11.21 p.m. covering seven stations in just 20 minutes. The BMRCL stated that the heart was carried inside Train ID 12, Train Set 29, accompanied by the hospital’s medical team. To ensure smooth movement, the Assistant Security Officer coordinated with the Sparsh team and metro security personnel, making special arrangements to avoid delays and provide a safe corridor for the critical transfer. Bengaluru Metro facilitates transportation of donor heart from Goraguntepalya to Bommasandra A live human heart arranged by Sparsh Hospital was transported via Namma Metro from Yeshwanthpur station to South End Circle station en route to Apollo Hospital on September 11, 2025. The organ was accompanied by the hospital’s medical team. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement In August, for the first time, Namma Metro had successfully facilitated the transportation of an organ. A donated human liver, meant for transplantation, was transported from Vydehi Hospital at Whitefield to Sparsh Hospital at R.R. Nagar. The operation was executed using a combination of ambulance and metro, significantly reducing travel time during peak traffic hours. After its first organ transport in August, #Bengaluru 's Namma Metro again facilitated an organ transport on Sept 11. articles.title: De-notification of MSMER-2023 removes overlapping procedures, but will it safeguard standards of medical education?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Under MSMER-2023, there was a defined escalation path; now, action depends on MARB assessments being initiated, completed and acted upon within a reasonable timeframe

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The National Medical Commission (NMC) has de-notified and withdrawn the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations, 2023 (MSMER-2023) where medical colleges were liable to face penalty fines for violations of educational standards and infrastructure requirements at medical colleges. Earlier reports in The Hindu stated NMC’s withdrawal of MSMER-2023 weakens accountability in medical education by removing provisions to fine individual faculty members and administrators up to ₹5 lakh for submitting false information. Although the Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB) can still penalise institutions up to ₹1 crore under separate regulations, institutional penalties may be less effective in deterring individual misconduct. Misleading faculty declarations, inflated patient records, or inadequate clinical training going undetected could ultimately put patients at risk. The NMC justified the withdrawal by arguing that MSMER created overlapping assessment powers with MARB. However, scrapping the regulations entirely raises questions about the necessity of this move, particularly when non-compliance remains common and transparency in medical education is inadequate. Moreover, conflicting appeal deadlines under MARB regulations and the NMC Act could lead to legal disputes and delay enforcement. Ultimately, the NMC must clarify whether the existing regulatory mechanisms are being effectively enforced and whether their outcomes are publicly accessible without which the withdrawal of MSMER risks appearing to be a relaxation of regulatory oversight rather than a simplification of rules. Medical experts have further warned that deterrence against practices such as ghost faculty and fabricated patient records would potentially expose students and institutions to greater malpractice and mismanagement. While some experts support the removal of regulatory duplication, they emphasise that effective oversight depends on rigorous verification, transparent reporting, consistent penalties and time-bound enforcement. The NMC must therefore demonstrate that MARB can enforce standards as effectively as the withdrawn framework; otherwise, regulatory rationalisation risks becoming a dilution of accountability.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The NMC has clarified that the MSMER introduced a parallel mechanism through which the undergraduate and postgraduate boards could assess institutions, thereby encroaching on the MARB’s mandate. While talking to The Hindu , NMC officials said the denotification is aimed at simplifying regulatory procedures and eliminating overlapping responsibilities, without compromising the quality of medical education.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 De-notification of MSMER-2023 removes overlapping procedures, but will it safeguard standards of medical education?

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 03:52:50 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Under MSMER-2023, there was a defined escalation path; now, action depends on MARB assessments being initiated, completed and acted upon within a reasonable timeframe

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The National Medical Commission (NMC) has de-notified and withdrawn the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations, 2023 (MSMER-2023) where medical colleges were liable to face penalty fines for violations of educational standards and infrastructure requirements at medical colleges. Earlier reports in The Hindu stated NMC’s withdrawal of MSMER-2023 weakens accountability in medical education by removing provisions to fine individual faculty members and administrators up to ₹5 lakh for submitting false information. Although the Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB) can still penalise institutions up to ₹1 crore under separate regulations, institutional penalties may be less effective in deterring individual misconduct. Misleading faculty declarations, inflated patient records, or inadequate clinical training going undetected could ultimately put patients at risk. The NMC justified the withdrawal by arguing that MSMER created overlapping assessment powers with MARB. However, scrapping the regulations entirely raises questions about the necessity of this move, particularly when non-compliance remains common and transparency in medical education is inadequate. Moreover, conflicting appeal deadlines under MARB regulations and the NMC Act could lead to legal disputes and delay enforcement. Ultimately, the NMC must clarify whether the existing regulatory mechanisms are being effectively enforced and whether their outcomes are publicly accessible without which the withdrawal of MSMER risks appearing to be a relaxation of regulatory oversight rather than a simplification of rules. Medical experts have further warned that deterrence against practices such as ghost faculty and fabricated patient records would potentially expose students and institutions to greater malpractice and mismanagement. While some experts support the removal of regulatory duplication, they emphasise that effective oversight depends on rigorous verification, transparent reporting, consistent penalties and time-bound enforcement. The NMC must therefore demonstrate that MARB can enforce standards as effectively as the withdrawn framework; otherwise, regulatory rationalisation risks becoming a dilution of accountability.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The NMC has clarified that the MSMER introduced a parallel mechanism through which the undergraduate and postgraduate boards could assess institutions, thereby encroaching on the MARB’s mandate. While talking to The Hindu , NMC officials said the denotification is aimed at simplifying regulatory procedures and eliminating overlapping responsibilities, without compromising the quality of medical education.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Enforcement (Noun)
सख्ती से कानून लागू करना — किसी नियम या आदेश का ज़मीनी स्तर पर पालन करवाना।
✓ Syn: Implementation, Execution, Administration  |  ✖ Ant: Neglect, Abandonment, Waiver
Relaxation (Noun)
नियमों में ढील या छूट — किसी कड़े प्रतिबंध को थोड़े समय के लिए हल्का करना।
✓ Syn: Moderation, Easing, Leniency  |  ✖ Ant: Strictness, Tightening, Rigidity
Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Accountability (Noun)
जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।
✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "De-notification of MSMER-2023 removes overlapping procedures, but will it safeguard standards of medical education?", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Under MSMER-2023, there was a defined escalation path; now, action depends on MARB assessments being initiated, completed and acted upon within a...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'De-notification of MSMER-2023 removes overlappin' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'De-notification of MSMER-2023 removes overlap' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'De-notification of MSMER-2023 removes overlap' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Under MSMER-2023, there was a defined escalation path; now, action depends on MARB assessments being initiated, completed and acted upon within a..." (Hinglish Arth: एमएसएमईआर-2023 के तहत, एक परिभाषित वृद्धि पथ था; अब, कार्रवाई एमएआरबी आकलन शुरू करने, पूरा करने और उचित समय सीमा के भीतर कार्रवाई करने पर निर्भर करती है)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "De-notification of MSMER-2023 removes overlapping procedures, but will it safeguard standards of medical education?"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. While talking to The Hindu , NMC officials said the denotification is aimed at simplifying regulatory procedures and eliminating overlapping...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "While talking to The Hindu , NMC officials said the denotification is aimed at simplifying regulatory procedures and eliminating overlapping..." • 1. Core Context & Background: Under MSMER-2023, there was a defined escalation path; now, action depends on MARB assessments being initiated, completed and acted upon within a reasonable timeframe
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The National Medical Commission (NMC) has de-notified and withdrawn the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations, 2023 (MSMER-2023) where medical colleges were liable to face penalty fines for violations of educational standards and infrastructure requirements at medical colleges. Earlier reports in The Hindu stated NMC’s withdrawal of MSMER-2023 weakens accountability in medical education by removing provisions to fine individual faculty members and administrators up to ₹5 lakh for submitting false information. Although the Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB) can still penalise institutions up to ₹1 crore under separate regulations, institutional penalties may be less effective in deterring individual misconduct. Misleading faculty declarations, inflated patient records, or inadequate clinical training going undetected could ultimately put patients at risk. The NMC justified the withdrawal by arguing that MSMER created overlapping assessment powers with MARB. However, scrapping the regulations entirely raises questions about the necessity of this move, particularly when non-compliance remains common and transparency in medical education is inadequate. Moreover, conflicting appeal deadlines under MARB regulations and the NMC Act could lead to legal disputes and delay enforcement. Ultimately, the NMC must clarify whether the existing regulatory mechanisms are being effectively enforced and whether their outcomes are publicly accessible without which the withdrawal of MSMER risks appearing to be a relaxation of regulatory oversight rather than a simplification of rules. Medical experts have further warned that deterrence against practices such as ghost faculty and fabricated patient records would potentially expose students and institutions to greater malpractice and mismanagement. While some experts support the removal of regulatory duplication, they emphasise that effective oversight depends on rigorous verification, transparent reporting, consistent penalties and time-bound enforcement. The NMC must therefore demonstrate that MARB can enforce standards as effectively as the withdrawn framework; otherwise, regulatory rationalisation risks becoming a dilution of accountability.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The NMC has clarified that the MSMER introduced a parallel mechanism through which the undergraduate and postgraduate boards could assess institutions, thereby encroaching on the MARB’s mandate. While talking to The Hindu , NMC officials said the denotification is aimed at simplifying regulatory procedures and eliminating overlapping responsibilities, without compromising the quality of medical education.

articles.title: GTA VI is here, and India has taken the day off

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Grand Theft Auto VI is a homecoming, and this time a good part of the city was built in Bengaluru

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: This week, Grand Theft Auto VI landed on Blinkit, in a collectible box available in select areas across 11 cities. There is no disc inside, only a download code, because Rockstar is selling the game purely as a download, even in stores. That makes for instant gratification of a new kind: the most anticipated game in years can now reach your doorstep in minutes, about as quickly as a loaf of bread, with the code ready to redeem the moment it arrives. Blinkit co-founder Albinder Dhindsa announced the offering on X on November 18, noting that it had taken 13 years for the game to arrive. It is a very 2026 way to launch a game, and an apt one, given that Grand Theft Auto has always found its way to Indian players through whichever door happened to be open. The game itself costs ₹5,999 for the Standard Edition and ₹7,499 for the Ultimate Edition on both PlayStation and Xbox, which is almost exactly double what Grand Theft Auto V cost here at launch. In dollars, though, Indian buyers pay about US$63 for the Standard Edition versus the $79.99 charged in the United States, and pre-order customers also receive the Vintage Vice City Pack. It is on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S only for now, with no PC version announced, which is a shift for a series so many Indians first met on a computer, though Grand Theft Auto V took the same route and reached PC in 2015. In solidarity, consumer electronics brand boAt offered employees an optional day off on November 19, announcing it with the caption Out of office. Into Vice City. In Chennai, interior design firm Inde by ChairsCarte declared a holiday for its staff, interns and freelancers, calling it “just a day off for a game we’ve waited years for”. For a generation of Indian players, the first port of call was the neighbourhood cyber café. Vice City and San Andreas, which defined the series in the early 2000s, were among the first open worlds many Indians explored, playing on rented computers by the hour, often between rounds of Counter-Strike, long before gaming became a career in India. San Andreas also gave us cheat codes, strings of nonsense such as HESOYAM, which replenished health, armour and cash in one go. For those who grew up typing them, they remain shorthand for nostalgia. Even Indians who have never owned a copy know the series, thanks to its meme culture. The grey-and-red Wasted screen from GTA V, which appears when a character dies, has spent years slapped onto videos of people and animals spectacularly failing at something. Big Smoke’s exasperated yell at CJ for losing a train in San Andreas became so widely shared that Rockstar later named a GTA V trophy Better Than CJ in its honour. But the longest-running joke was about the wait. As the sequel failed to materialise, “We got X before GTA 6” became the Internet’s way of reacting to anything improbable. India took to it enthusiastically, with electronics retailer Croma fuelling another round when the game was delayed to November 19, 2026.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Hindu Weekend / gaming and lottery / lifestyle and leisure / technology (general) / games / leisure (general)

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #30 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 GTA VI is here, and India has taken the day off

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 03:21:05 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Grand Theft Auto VI is a homecoming, and this time a good part of the city was built in Bengaluru

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: This week, Grand Theft Auto VI landed on Blinkit, in a collectible box available in select areas across 11 cities. There is no disc inside, only a download code, because Rockstar is selling the game purely as a download, even in stores. That makes for instant gratification of a new kind: the most anticipated game in years can now reach your doorstep in minutes, about as quickly as a loaf of bread, with the code ready to redeem the moment it arrives. Blinkit co-founder Albinder Dhindsa announced the offering on X on November 18, noting that it had taken 13 years for the game to arrive. It is a very 2026 way to launch a game, and an apt one, given that Grand Theft Auto has always found its way to Indian players through whichever door happened to be open. The game itself costs ₹5,999 for the Standard Edition and ₹7,499 for the Ultimate Edition on both PlayStation and Xbox, which is almost exactly double what Grand Theft Auto V cost here at launch. In dollars, though, Indian buyers pay about US$63 for the Standard Edition versus the $79.99 charged in the United States, and pre-order customers also receive the Vintage Vice City Pack. It is on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S only for now, with no PC version announced, which is a shift for a series so many Indians first met on a computer, though Grand Theft Auto V took the same route and reached PC in 2015. In solidarity, consumer electronics brand boAt offered employees an optional day off on November 19, announcing it with the caption Out of office. Into Vice City. In Chennai, interior design firm Inde by ChairsCarte declared a holiday for its staff, interns and freelancers, calling it “just a day off for a game we’ve waited years for”. For a generation of Indian players, the first port of call was the neighbourhood cyber café. Vice City and San Andreas, which defined the series in the early 2000s, were among the first open worlds many Indians explored, playing on rented computers by the hour, often between rounds of Counter-Strike, long before gaming became a career in India. San Andreas also gave us cheat codes, strings of nonsense such as HESOYAM, which replenished health, armour and cash in one go. For those who grew up typing them, they remain shorthand for nostalgia. Even Indians who have never owned a copy know the series, thanks to its meme culture. The grey-and-red Wasted screen from GTA V, which appears when a character dies, has spent years slapped onto videos of people and animals spectacularly failing at something. Big Smoke’s exasperated yell at CJ for losing a train in San Andreas became so widely shared that Rockstar later named a GTA V trophy Better Than CJ in its honour. But the longest-running joke was about the wait. As the sequel failed to materialise, “We got X before GTA 6” became the Internet’s way of reacting to anything improbable. India took to it enthusiastically, with electronics retailer Croma fuelling another round when the game was delayed to November 19, 2026.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Hindu Weekend / gaming and lottery / lifestyle and leisure / technology (general) / games / leisure (general)

articles.title: Iran rules out talks with U.S. until its seven conditions are met
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Iran also said three oil tankers had struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire despite U.S. aerial protection

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Iran reiterated Tuesday (November 24, 2026) that it would not hold talks with the United States to end the conflict, saying that seven conditions must be met first, though it didn't specify the conditions. Iran also said three oil tankers had struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire despite U.S. aerial protection. Meanwhile, at least nine Palestinians were killed in several Israeli strikes in Gaza, local officials said. Iran's chief negotiator and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Tuesday (November 24, 2026) that Tehran wouldn't negotiate with the U.S. "until Iran's seven conditions are met,” according to Iranian state television. Iranian authorities haven't publicly stated what those conditions are. But Iranian state media have said they include the lifting of sanctions, the ending of the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports and the release of seized Iranian assets. He also warned that Iran would “shift the geographical scope of the conflict should the enemy make a mistake.” The naval arm of Iran's Revolutionary Guard said the three oil tankers struck the naval mines because they were “in violation of regulations” regarding passage through the Strait of Hormuz. The Guard's navy said in a post on Telegram Monday (November 23, 2026) that the strait “is not a place to test unauthorised routes or to disregard maritime warnings.” It said the tankers were “engulfed in flames” after hitting the mines despite being under U.S. aerial escort.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: At least nine people were killed in four Israeli strikes Monday night (November 23, 2026) and Tuesday morning (November 24, 2026), officials in Gaza said. Among those killed was a senior security official in the Hamas-run government's Interior Ministry.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #21 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 Iran rules out talks with U.S. until its seven conditions are met

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 11:06:11 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Iran also said three oil tankers had struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire despite U.S. aerial protection

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Iran reiterated Tuesday (November 24, 2026) that it would not hold talks with the United States to end the conflict, saying that seven conditions must be met first, though it didn't specify the conditions. Iran also said three oil tankers had struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire despite U.S. aerial protection. Meanwhile, at least nine Palestinians were killed in several Israeli strikes in Gaza, local officials said. Iran's chief negotiator and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Tuesday (November 24, 2026) that Tehran wouldn't negotiate with the U.S. "until Iran's seven conditions are met,” according to Iranian state television. Iranian authorities haven't publicly stated what those conditions are. But Iranian state media have said they include the lifting of sanctions, the ending of the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports and the release of seized Iranian assets. He also warned that Iran would “shift the geographical scope of the conflict should the enemy make a mistake.” The naval arm of Iran's Revolutionary Guard said the three oil tankers struck the naval mines because they were “in violation of regulations” regarding passage through the Strait of Hormuz. The Guard's navy said in a post on Telegram Monday (November 23, 2026) that the strait “is not a place to test unauthorised routes or to disregard maritime warnings.” It said the tankers were “engulfed in flames” after hitting the mines despite being under U.S. aerial escort.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: At least nine people were killed in four Israeli strikes Monday night (November 23, 2026) and Tuesday morning (November 24, 2026), officials in Gaza said. Among those killed was a senior security official in the Hamas-run government's Interior Ministry.

A. Iran also said three oil tankers had struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire despite U.S.

articles.title: Former members say EPG report was ‘highly positive’ for India-Nepal ties
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Their reaction comes a day after Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri termed the report of India-Nepal Eminent Persons Group “not relevant”

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A day after Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri termed the report of the India-Nepal Eminent Persons Group (EPG) “not relevant”, arguing that India will take a “forward looking” approach regarding boundary issues with Nepal, a former member of the EPG has said the report was “highly positive” for both India and Nepal and that it was “odd” that the group did not get a chance to present the report to the Government of India. “The EPG report was produced after extensive research and field visits. We visited Visakhapatnam and other ports that are of interest to Nepal and spoke with many stakeholders before compiling the report and there are interesting recommendations in the report that could be of great use for India and Nepal and it was highly positive for Delhi-Kathmandu relations,” said Mahendra P. Lama, former professor of Jawaharlal Nehru University, who served as a member of the EPG. ALSO WATCH India-Nepal ties: What does Modi-Balen partnership promise? | Above the Fold | Nov 23, 2026 The EPG returned to the spotlight on Monday (November 23, 2026) when Mr. Misri announced in a press conference held after the visit of Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah that New Delhi would adopt a “forward-looking” approach to the border issues. “The leaders have given a direction as part of the overall very forward-looking discussions that have been held today for the foreign secretaries to take the task forward. We will do so in a forward-looking manner, taking inspiration from the vision document and from the directions and indeed the spirit in which the discussions were held. I would say that EPG is in the past. We are not looking backward,” said Mr. Misri in response to a question. He described the EPG report as “not relevant”. Former Nepali ambassador and coordinator of the EPG on the Nepali side, Bhek Bahadur Thapa, described the EPG report as a step forward for the bilateral consultation process. “It was not a unilateral document, it was a document created through bilateral consultation among experts appointed by New Delhi and Kathmandu,” said Mr. Thapa, who has also served as Foreign Minister of Nepal during 2004-05. The EPG report dealing with a broad spectrum of India-Nepal relations, including the Kalapani dispute and the 1950 India-Nepal Friendship Treaty was completed in 2018 but it remained under sealed covers. “It is odd that the report could not be launched here in Delhi. The Nepali side said the EPG report should be unveiled first by the Indian Prime Minister and on the same day we were supposed to return to Kathmandu for the report’s unveiling by the Nepali Prime Minister, “ said Prof. Lama, informing that they made a mistake as Kathmandu could have also unveiled the report first. “Our recommendations now can be accessed by other stakeholders in Kathmandu and I don’t think that is a positive thing,” said Mr. Lama. The EPG was institutionalised according to an understanding that was reached during the delegation-level talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and former Nepali Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli in February 2016. The visit of Mr. Oli took place against the backdrop of months-long blockade on Nepal-India border that Kathmandu said was imposed by India but India blamed the Madhesi agitators of Nepal for imposing the blockade that hindered flow of essential items such as cooking gas into Nepal. During the time of its existence, a part of the Institute of Defence Studies and Analyses (IDSA) in Delhi served as the secretariat for the EPG. The then Director General of the IDSA Jayant Prasad was also part of the EPG.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Incidentally, officials who are currently playing key roles in India-Nepal relations were also involved in the EPG process. Former members recounted that the newly appointed Indian ambassador to Nepal Sudhakar Dalela was the Joint Secretary (North) in the Ministry of External Affairs and was part of the EPG process during 2016-18. That apart, the new Nepali ambassador to India Nischal Nath Pandey also was part of the EPG process in Kathmandu.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #22 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 Former members say EPG report was ‘highly positive’ for India-Nepal ties

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 11:01:38 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Their reaction comes a day after Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri termed the report of India-Nepal Eminent Persons Group “not relevant”

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A day after Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri termed the report of the India-Nepal Eminent Persons Group (EPG) “not relevant”, arguing that India will take a “forward looking” approach regarding boundary issues with Nepal, a former member of the EPG has said the report was “highly positive” for both India and Nepal and that it was “odd” that the group did not get a chance to present the report to the Government of India. “The EPG report was produced after extensive research and field visits. We visited Visakhapatnam and other ports that are of interest to Nepal and spoke with many stakeholders before compiling the report and there are interesting recommendations in the report that could be of great use for India and Nepal and it was highly positive for Delhi-Kathmandu relations,” said Mahendra P. Lama, former professor of Jawaharlal Nehru University, who served as a member of the EPG. ALSO WATCH India-Nepal ties: What does Modi-Balen partnership promise? | Above the Fold | Nov 23, 2026 The EPG returned to the spotlight on Monday (November 23, 2026) when Mr. Misri announced in a press conference held after the visit of Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah that New Delhi would adopt a “forward-looking” approach to the border issues. “The leaders have given a direction as part of the overall very forward-looking discussions that have been held today for the foreign secretaries to take the task forward. We will do so in a forward-looking manner, taking inspiration from the vision document and from the directions and indeed the spirit in which the discussions were held. I would say that EPG is in the past. We are not looking backward,” said Mr. Misri in response to a question. He described the EPG report as “not relevant”. Former Nepali ambassador and coordinator of the EPG on the Nepali side, Bhek Bahadur Thapa, described the EPG report as a step forward for the bilateral consultation process. “It was not a unilateral document, it was a document created through bilateral consultation among experts appointed by New Delhi and Kathmandu,” said Mr. Thapa, who has also served as Foreign Minister of Nepal during 2004-05. The EPG report dealing with a broad spectrum of India-Nepal relations, including the Kalapani dispute and the 1950 India-Nepal Friendship Treaty was completed in 2018 but it remained under sealed covers. “It is odd that the report could not be launched here in Delhi. The Nepali side said the EPG report should be unveiled first by the Indian Prime Minister and on the same day we were supposed to return to Kathmandu for the report’s unveiling by the Nepali Prime Minister, “ said Prof. Lama, informing that they made a mistake as Kathmandu could have also unveiled the report first. “Our recommendations now can be accessed by other stakeholders in Kathmandu and I don’t think that is a positive thing,” said Mr. Lama. The EPG was institutionalised according to an understanding that was reached during the delegation-level talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and former Nepali Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli in February 2016. The visit of Mr. Oli took place against the backdrop of months-long blockade on Nepal-India border that Kathmandu said was imposed by India but India blamed the Madhesi agitators of Nepal for imposing the blockade that hindered flow of essential items such as cooking gas into Nepal. During the time of its existence, a part of the Institute of Defence Studies and Analyses (IDSA) in Delhi served as the secretariat for the EPG. The then Director General of the IDSA Jayant Prasad was also part of the EPG.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Incidentally, officials who are currently playing key roles in India-Nepal relations were also involved in the EPG process. Former members recounted that the newly appointed Indian ambassador to Nepal Sudhakar Dalela was the Joint Secretary (North) in the Ministry of External Affairs and was part of the EPG process during 2016-18. That apart, the new Nepali ambassador to India Nischal Nath Pandey also was part of the EPG process in Kathmandu.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Bilateral (Adjective)
द्विपक्षीय — दो देशों के बीच आपसी समझौता, व्यापार या कूटनीतिक बातचीत।
✓ Syn: Reciprocal, Two-sided, Mutual  |  ✖ Ant: Unilateral, Multilateral, One-way
Consultation (Noun)
परामर्श — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Consultation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Inspiration (Adjective / Verb)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Inspiration' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🌐 International & Geopolitics passage on "Former members say EPG report was ‘highly positive’ for India-Nepal ties", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Their reaction comes a day after Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri termed the report of India-Nepal Eminent Persons Group “not relevant”.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Former members say EPG report was ‘highly positi' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Former members say EPG report was ‘highly pos' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Former members say EPG report was ‘highly pos' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Their reaction comes a day after Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri termed the report of India-Nepal Eminent Persons Group “not relevant”." (Hinglish Arth: उनकी यह प्रतिक्रिया विदेश सचिव विक्रम मिस्री द्वारा भारत-नेपाल प्रतिष्ठित व्यक्ति समूह की रिपोर्ट को ''प्रासंगिक नहीं'' बताए जाने के एक दिन बाद आई है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Former members say EPG report was ‘highly positive’ for India-Nepal ties"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. That apart, the new Nepali ambassador to India Nischal Nath Pandey also was part of the EPG process in Kathmandu.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "That apart, the new Nepali ambassador to India Nischal Nath Pandey also was part of the EPG process in Kathmandu." (Hinglish Arth: इसके अलावा, भारत में नए नेपाली राजदूत निश्चल नाथ पांडे भी काठमांडू में ईपीजी प्रक्रिया का हिस्सा थे।)

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: A Russian nighttime attack on Zaporizhzhia in southern Ukraine has killed two civilians and wounded 48 others including four children

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A Russian nighttime attack on the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia killed two civilians and wounded 48 others, including four children, officials said Tuesday (November 24, 2026), as authorities in Ukraine and Libya debated the legitimacy of an unprecedented Ukrainian strike on a Russian warship docked in Benghazi. The Zaporizhzhia glide bomb attack destroyed a private house and partially destroyed a five-story apartment building, according to Mykhailo Semikin, the head of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Military Administration. The youngest wounded child was less than a year old, he said, adding that the others were ages 4, 6 and 16. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Tuesday (November 24, 2026) that the Ukrainian military is sending reinforcements to the Zaporizhzhia region, which lies on the roughly 1,250-kilometer (almost 800-mile) front line snaking through eastern and southern Ukraine. Russia and Ukraine have escalated their aerial strikes in recent months even as they engage in U.S.-mediated talks to end the war that began with Moscow’s full-scale invasion of its neighbor nearly five years ago. Mr. Zelenskyy noted in a speech that Ukraine needs 115 billion euros ($126 billion) in aid from foreign countries next year to keep up the fight. Funding of 90 billion euros ($98.7 billion) is already assured, he said, but Ukraine needs to find another 25 billion euros ($27.4 billion). The United Nations says the war has killed close to 18,000 Ukrainian civilians and wounded more than 57,000 others since the all-out war broke out on Feb. 24, 2022. Hundreds of thousands of soldiers from both sides are believed to have died on the battlefield. Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship in Libya Russia says four killed in major Ukraine drone barrage More than 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the war, according to an estimate by independent Russian news outlets Meduza and Mediazona, which have been tracking Russian military losses for several years.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: They said that they received a huge dataset earlier this month that was hacked from Russia’s state statistics agency Rosstat by Belarusian activist group Cyber Partisans and a Ukrainian hacker group, Silent Crow. They added projected deaths not yet recorded by Russian authorities.

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — उन्होंने कहा कि उन्हें इस महीने की शुरुआत में एक विशाल डेटासेट प्राप्त हुआ था जिसे बेलारूसी कार्यकर्ता समूह साइबर पार्टिसंस और एक यूक्रेनी हैकर समूह, साइलेंट क्रो द्वारा रूस की राज्य सांख्यिकी एजेंसी रोसस्टैट से हैक किया गया था।।

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A Russian nighttime attack on the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia killed two civilians and wounded 48 others, including four children, officials said Tuesday (November 24, 2026), as authorities in Ukraine and Libya debated the legitimacy of an unprecedented Ukrainian strike on a Russian warship docked in Benghazi. Mr. Zelenskyy noted in a speech that Ukraine needs 115 billion euros ($126 billion) in aid from foreign countries next year to keep up the fight. Funding of 90 billion euros ($98.7 billion) is already assured, he said, but Ukraine needs to find another 25 billion euros ($27.4 billion). articles.title: Yemen officials say strike on buses, trucks kills 26
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Yemen, one of the world's poorest countries, has become the most active front in the West Asia war, with the Iran-backed Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition exchanging frequent attacks

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: An airstrike on trucks and buses killed 26 people in Yemen's southwest, local officials told AFP on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), as the Houthis and government forces traded blame for the attack. Yemen, one of the world's poorest countries, has become the most active front in the West Asia war, with the Iran-backed Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition exchanging frequent attacks. Two officials said coalition warplanes struck Houthi vehicles on Monday (November 23, 2026) in Lahj province, where the group has advanced in recent weeks towards Aden, the government's interim capital. The aircraft "targeted two vehicles belonging to the Houthis at the moment when a truck and a bus were passing by, in an area considered a front line", one of the officials said, adding 12 Houthi fighters and 14 civilians were killed. The second official confirmed the death toll. Witnesses reported seeing charred bodies at the scene. The Houthis' military spokesman blamed the Saudi air force for the strike, saying it would not go "unanswered". But government forces said the Houthis carried out the attack. The pro-Iran group targeted "civilian vehicles bearing no military markings, on a road that is a vital artery for the population", government forces spokesman Majed al-Nazli said. Separate strikes on Monday (November 23, 2026) killed 17 people and destroyed several buildings in the coastal province of Hodeida, the Houthis' telecommunications ministry said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Yemen, embroiled in more than a decade of civil war, was sucked into the wider U.S.-Iran conflict in July when a truce between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government unravelled.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 Yemen officials say strike on buses, trucks kills 26

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 10:38:30 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Yemen, one of the world's poorest countries, has become the most active front in the West Asia war, with the Iran-backed Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition exchanging frequent attacks

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: An airstrike on trucks and buses killed 26 people in Yemen's southwest, local officials told AFP on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), as the Houthis and government forces traded blame for the attack. Yemen, one of the world's poorest countries, has become the most active front in the West Asia war, with the Iran-backed Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition exchanging frequent attacks. Two officials said coalition warplanes struck Houthi vehicles on Monday (November 23, 2026) in Lahj province, where the group has advanced in recent weeks towards Aden, the government's interim capital. The aircraft "targeted two vehicles belonging to the Houthis at the moment when a truck and a bus were passing by, in an area considered a front line", one of the officials said, adding 12 Houthi fighters and 14 civilians were killed. The second official confirmed the death toll. Witnesses reported seeing charred bodies at the scene. The Houthis' military spokesman blamed the Saudi air force for the strike, saying it would not go "unanswered". But government forces said the Houthis carried out the attack. The pro-Iran group targeted "civilian vehicles bearing no military markings, on a road that is a vital artery for the population", government forces spokesman Majed al-Nazli said. Separate strikes on Monday (November 23, 2026) killed 17 people and destroyed several buildings in the coastal province of Hodeida, the Houthis' telecommunications ministry said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Yemen, embroiled in more than a decade of civil war, was sucked into the wider U.S.-Iran conflict in July when a truce between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government unravelled.

articles.title: Indian space companies sign largest-of-its-kind deal on satellite systems
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Bellatrix Aerospace to supply in-space propulsion systems for GalaxEye’s 30 satellites

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Indian space companies GalaxEye and Bellatrix Aerospace on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) signed a multi-year contract in which Bellatrix Aerospace will supply in-space propulsion systems for the next 30 satellites GalaxEye is building. This made the deal the “largest business-to-business order” one Indian private space company has placed with another since the space sector opened to private players in 2020, a press release noted. While private companies have participated in India’s space sector since inception, it has usually been as suppliers to the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). The GalaxEye-Bellatrix deal was unveiled at the 5th India International Space Conclave, organised by the Indian Space Association (ISpA). The financial details of the contract were not disclosed. GalaxEye is building the world’s first OptoSAR satellite constellation. OptoSAR is a proprietary imaging technology that allows customers to see any place on Earth through clouds, smoke, and darkness. Bellatrix builds the thrusters that steer and position satellites once they reach orbit, with hardware already flight-tested on ISRO missions. “OptoSAR satellites are demanding customers. They need precise, repeatable orbits across a whole constellation, not a single demonstration. Our thrusters have already fired in orbit on ISRO missions, and we have built the production lines to deliver that same performance at constellation scale,” Rohan M. Ganapathy, co-founder and CEO of Bellatrix Aerospace, said in a statement. Bellatrix makes electric and green propulsion systems for satellites and orbital transfer vehicles. Mission Drishti, launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 on May 3, 2026, became the world’s first OptoSAR satellite in orbit. It validated GalaxEye’s spacecraft deployment, attitude control, onboard computing and in-house mission operations before contact was lost after a geomagnetic storm, the company stated. In September, the Department of Science and Technology’s Technology Development Board committed ₹63.84 crore from the Government of India’s Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund for GalaxEye’s next multi-sensor satellite, which targets imagery sharper than 0.5 metres. Sourcing propulsion from a partner in the same city gives GalaxEye closer engineering control and shorter lead times as it builds that satellite. “Drishti taught us that every critical system on a satellite has to be one we can see, test and improve up close,” Suyash Singh, co-founder and CEO of GalaxEye, said in a statement. ISRO chairman V. Narayanan said that private industry was now indispensable to India’s space ecosystem. “Today, we are extremely happy that 440 start-up companies are working in the space area. Whenever a launch vehicle lifts off or we place a satellite, 70-80% of the budget is pumped into the Indian industry. Without the support of Indian industry, we would not have reached the present level.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Other officials, however, pointed out while India was putting in place a system to increase capacity, it had to work towards increasing demand for products from the private space ecosystem. “The first phase of India’s space reforms opened the sector and created an institutional framework for private participation. Now India has to work on generating heavy demand. I have less concern about capacity being created; I see a bigger need for demand to be created. The second is to have enough money coming into the sector, and number three, to have procedures at all levels. Space is not a sector that is going to give you a payback in six months or nine months. Perseverance is required, and the government must continue to have policy stability,” said Pawan Goenka, chairman, InSpace, India’s single-window regulatory and promotional body for the private space sector.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #25 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 Indian space companies sign largest-of-its-kind deal on satellite systems

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 09:27:58 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Bellatrix Aerospace to supply in-space propulsion systems for GalaxEye’s 30 satellites

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Indian space companies GalaxEye and Bellatrix Aerospace on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) signed a multi-year contract in which Bellatrix Aerospace will supply in-space propulsion systems for the next 30 satellites GalaxEye is building. This made the deal the “largest business-to-business order” one Indian private space company has placed with another since the space sector opened to private players in 2020, a press release noted. While private companies have participated in India’s space sector since inception, it has usually been as suppliers to the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). The GalaxEye-Bellatrix deal was unveiled at the 5th India International Space Conclave, organised by the Indian Space Association (ISpA). The financial details of the contract were not disclosed. GalaxEye is building the world’s first OptoSAR satellite constellation. OptoSAR is a proprietary imaging technology that allows customers to see any place on Earth through clouds, smoke, and darkness. Bellatrix builds the thrusters that steer and position satellites once they reach orbit, with hardware already flight-tested on ISRO missions. “OptoSAR satellites are demanding customers. They need precise, repeatable orbits across a whole constellation, not a single demonstration. Our thrusters have already fired in orbit on ISRO missions, and we have built the production lines to deliver that same performance at constellation scale,” Rohan M. Ganapathy, co-founder and CEO of Bellatrix Aerospace, said in a statement. Bellatrix makes electric and green propulsion systems for satellites and orbital transfer vehicles. Mission Drishti, launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 on May 3, 2026, became the world’s first OptoSAR satellite in orbit. It validated GalaxEye’s spacecraft deployment, attitude control, onboard computing and in-house mission operations before contact was lost after a geomagnetic storm, the company stated. In September, the Department of Science and Technology’s Technology Development Board committed ₹63.84 crore from the Government of India’s Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund for GalaxEye’s next multi-sensor satellite, which targets imagery sharper than 0.5 metres. Sourcing propulsion from a partner in the same city gives GalaxEye closer engineering control and shorter lead times as it builds that satellite. “Drishti taught us that every critical system on a satellite has to be one we can see, test and improve up close,” Suyash Singh, co-founder and CEO of GalaxEye, said in a statement. ISRO chairman V. Narayanan said that private industry was now indispensable to India’s space ecosystem. “Today, we are extremely happy that 440 start-up companies are working in the space area. Whenever a launch vehicle lifts off or we place a satellite, 70-80% of the budget is pumped into the Indian industry. Without the support of Indian industry, we would not have reached the present level.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Other officials, however, pointed out while India was putting in place a system to increase capacity, it had to work towards increasing demand for products from the private space ecosystem. “The first phase of India’s space reforms opened the sector and created an institutional framework for private participation. Now India has to work on generating heavy demand. I have less concern about capacity being created; I see a bigger need for demand to be created. The second is to have enough money coming into the sector, and number three, to have procedures at all levels. Space is not a sector that is going to give you a payback in six months or nine months. Perseverance is required, and the government must continue to have policy stability,” said Pawan Goenka, chairman, InSpace, India’s single-window regulatory and promotional body for the private space sector.

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "Indian space companies sign largest-of-its-kind deal on satellite systems", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Bellatrix Aerospace to supply in-space propulsion systems for GalaxEye’s 30 satellites.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Indian space companies sign largest-of-its-kind ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Indian space companies sign largest-of-its-ki' should be permanently discontinued.

articles.summary: 1. Core Context & Background: Bellatrix Aerospace to supply in-space propulsion systems for GalaxEye’s 30 satellites
articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Bellatrix Aerospace to supply in-space propulsion systems for GalaxEye’s 30 satellites
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Indian space companies GalaxEye and Bellatrix Aerospace on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) signed a multi-year contract in which Bellatrix Aerospace will supply in-space propulsion systems for the next 30 satellites GalaxEye is building. This made the deal the “largest business-to-business order” one Indian private space company has placed with another since the space sector opened to private players in 2020, a press release noted. While private companies have participated in India’s space sector since inception, it has usually been as suppliers to the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). The GalaxEye-Bellatrix deal was unveiled at the 5th India International Space Conclave, organised by the Indian Space Association (ISpA). The financial details of the contract were not disclosed. GalaxEye is building the world’s first OptoSAR satellite constellation. OptoSAR is a proprietary imaging technology that allows customers to see any place on Earth through clouds, smoke, and darkness. Bellatrix builds the thrusters that steer and position satellites once they reach orbit, with hardware already flight-tested on ISRO missions. “OptoSAR satellites are demanding customers. They need precise, repeatable orbits across a whole constellation, not a single demonstration. Our thrusters have already fired in orbit on ISRO missions, and we have built the production lines to deliver that same performance at constellation scale,” Rohan M. Ganapathy, co-founder and CEO of Bellatrix Aerospace, said in a statement. Bellatrix makes electric and green propulsion systems for satellites and orbital transfer vehicles. Mission Drishti, launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 on May 3, 2026, became the world’s first OptoSAR satellite in orbit. It validated GalaxEye’s spacecraft deployment, attitude control, onboard computing and in-house mission operations before contact was lost after a geomagnetic storm, the company stated. In September, the Department of Science and Technology’s Technology Development Board committed ₹63.84 crore from the Government of India’s Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund for GalaxEye’s next multi-sensor satellite, which targets imagery sharper than 0.5 metres. Sourcing propulsion from a partner in the same city gives GalaxEye closer engineering control and shorter lead times as it builds that satellite. “Drishti taught us that every critical system on a satellite has to be one we can see, test and improve up close,” Suyash Singh, co-founder and CEO of GalaxEye, said in a statement. ISRO chairman V. Narayanan said that private industry was now indispensable to India’s space ecosystem. “Today, we are extremely happy that 440 start-up companies are working in the space area. Whenever a launch vehicle lifts off or we place a satellite, 70-80% of the budget is pumped into the Indian industry. Without the support of Indian industry, we would not have reached the present level.”
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Other officials, however, pointed out while India was putting in place a system to increase capacity, it had to work towards increasing demand for products from the private space ecosystem. “The first phase of India’s space reforms opened the sector and created an institutional framework for private participation. Now India has to work on generating heavy demand. I have less concern about capacity being created; I see a bigger need for demand to be created. The second is to have enough money coming into the sector, and number three, to have procedures at all levels. Space is not a sector that is going to give you a payback in six months or nine months. Perseverance is required, and the government must continue to have policy stability,” said Pawan Goenka, chairman, InSpace, India’s single-window regulatory and promotional body for the private space sector.

Gukesh, and his challenger, Javokhir Sindarov, produced chess of top quality, and the draw was a just result . Given that the Indian was playing with black pieces and that he had gone into the match as the less favoured of the two, Gukesh could be a little happier with the game than his Uzbek rival. The Chennai Grandmaster was in considerable time trouble on multiple occasions, but managed to solve his problems and found proper answers to the questions posed to him on the board by the confident Sindarov. The match has only begun, and there is plenty of chess left. It is a long match of 14 games, played in the classical time control, and the man who reaches 7.5 points will be the champion. The well-contested opening game would have given Gukesh, and his team comprising his coach and ‘seconds’, enough confidence, after several disappointing performances since he became the youngest World champion in history , at 18, by defeating China’s Ding Liren in Singapore two years ago. That match too had gone down the wire, with Gukesh winning the last of the 14 games, thanks to a terrible mistake towards the end by his rival. Sindarov is just six months older than Gukesh, making the Geneva match the youngest in the 140-year-old history of the World championship: both players are 20. It is remarkable that Gukesh has already seen the highs and lows of life at such a young age. For his opponent, the last one year has been better than a dream: from World No. 26 he has risen to No. 4. Chess is getting younger. The next World championship could also very well have two young contenders. Grandmasters are usually said to peak when they are around 30 and chess is one game that even older players have continued to excel in. Viswanathan Anand was 48 when he won the World rapid chess championship . The match between Gukesh and Sindarov has attracted considerable interest from across the sporting world. After the 1972 match between Boris Spassky and Bobby Fischer — the defining moment of world chess — the World championship has earned a reputation as one of the planet’s most important sporting events. No battle between two of the world’s most talented men in chess has ever disappointed.

1. Core Context & Background: BJP and SAD(B) cannot count on their support bases adding up

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Few parties understand the arithmetic of the first-past-the-post (FPTP) system, and the necessity for alliances in States where they are minor players, better than the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) . The BJP has never shied away from partnerships with little ideological cohesion if they keep it electorally relevant. India’s FPTP system is unforgiving to smaller parties in a crowded polity if their support base is limited and dispersed. Votes translate into seats only if the support crosses a certain threshold. In Punjab , the BJP, despite its best efforts, has remained confined to sections of urban Hindu voters. Even after years of poaching leaders from the perennially fractious Congress , and after polling nearly a fifth of the vote in the 2024 general election without winning a seat, it realises that it cannot be relevant without a partner with a wider rural base. The Shiromani Akali Dal (Badal) walked out of the BJP -led National Democratic Alliance in 2020 over the Centre’s farm laws, which were later repealed, as the farmers’ agitation threatened its base in rural Punjab. But much water has flowed down the many rivers of the northern State since then. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has consolidated its hold in a crowded political space and is set to complete a full term. The Panthic vote, which used to be the SAD(B)’s core support base, has now fragmented. The SAD(B) appears to believe that it can regain ground only by expanding beyond its Panthic and rural constituencies, and that the farmers’ anger against the BJP is baggage from the past. It is this expedient calculation that now binds the two parties, despite six years of bitter attacks against each other. And it is also why the Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has pointedly called the SAD(B) the “big brother” in Punjab after sealing the alliance. The SAD(B)’s calculation may not work out as well as it hopes it would. Farmers’ anger against the BJP-led Centre has not entirely dissipated in rural Punjab. In earlier alliances, the two parties transferred votes to each other effectively, partly because their voters had fewer alternatives. But a revived Congress and an entrenched AAP have shown that they can win over urban Hindu voters wary of the Akalis and rural voters who are not inclined to back parties allied with the BJP. That these two sections will simply add up for the alliance is not certain. At best, the alliance consolidates enough of the anti-AAP vote to make this a clear three-cornered contest. Punjab is a sensitive border State and one of India’s granaries. It is also among India’s most indebted States, with a stagnating agrarian economy and a government that has expanded welfare expenditure despite strained finances. It needs a serious competition of ideas on what welfare it can afford and how to revive growth. The SAD(B)-BJP alliance , with its Panthic appeal on one side and Hindu consolidation on the other, instead offers a rehash of familiar identity politics. With AAP failing to deliver on governance, and the Congress stuck in its old ways, Punjab’s voters will have to decide who they dislike the least.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: political parties / Bharatiya Janata Party / Punjab / voting / Indian National Congress / General Elections 2024 / Shiromani Akali Dal / Aam Aadmi Party / agriculture / economy / welfare

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: While Karnataka has spent years disputing motorcycle owners’ right to carry paying passengers, Bengaluru — with the dubious distinction of having one of the world’s highest travel times per unit distance — struggles with inadequate public transport capacity and lacklustre intermediate options. The Supreme Court ruling on November 20 to dismiss Karnataka’s appeal was thus straightforward, allowing motorcycles to be registered as transport vehicles. The State has often called bike taxis unsafe, yet has not improved the prospects of safer options. Earlier this year, the Centre for Science and Environment estimated the number of buses in urban centres nationwide to be 70% short of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs benchmark and that 400 cities with populations between a lakh and 10 lakh altogether lacked organised bus services. In March, the BMTC reported a fleet of around 7,000 buses in Bengaluru, versus the 13,000 by 2025 envisaged by the Comprehensive Mobility Plan. Expanding the number of Metro stations also creates more demand for travel to and from stations, but the operating costs of the public transport corporation expected to serve that demand are not covered by the resulting increase in rail ridership. Overall, Karnataka has struggled to set up a consistent transport policy. An expert committee recommended against bike taxis in Bengaluru for first- and last-mile connectivity and in favour of better walking infrastructure and bicycle rentals in 2019, only for the State to launch the electric bike-taxi scheme in 2021, then rescind it in 2024 over safety concerns and drivers’ disputes. The market for short booked journeys is also dysfunctional. But while allowing bike taxis could temper autorickshaw fares, the State must investigate drivers’ operating costs, the difference between the paid and the received amounts, and prevent large platforms from exploiting the market. Finally, while the Union Road Transport Ministry has reported that 46.2% of all road deaths involved two-wheeler users, two-wheelers’ safety relative to autorickshaws and cabs, by the number and distance of journeys, is unclear. The State should require aggregators to report injuries and fatalities and investigate the consequences of drivers’ earnings being linked to the number of trips undertaken. The Union government’s 2025 Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines already address passenger security, fares, and insurance while allowing States to authorise privately registered motorcycles through aggregators. Karnataka should exercise this additional power. A large national programme is required to address funding for public transport, which is necessary even when it is not immediately profitable.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Developed nations must bear much of the cost of carbon emissions

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: COP31 ended in Antalya, Türkiye, with a whimper. The 190-odd countries that had convened for nearly 12 days — a close to 50-hour overshoot — failed to agree on an overarching political statement , called a cover text, that acts as a stepping stone to future, collective global action on climate change. Usually, cover texts evolve as a final synthesis of deliberations ; the COP31 leadership, helmed by Türkiye and Australia, thought it fit to push for a cover text early in the proceedings. The headline sought was a global electrification target: 35% of global final energy consumption will come from electricity by 2035, in the hope that this would reduce direct fossil fuel emissions. Ultimately, the cover text failed to pass muster because the European Union objected to the text’s lack of any explicit mention of ‘fossil fuel,’ let alone its phase-out. The COP process is arduously protracted as even a single country’s objection can stall progress. Country-blocks outside the EU, such as coalitions of the least developed countries, island nations, some South American countries — reportedly 130 countries — were also insistent on fossil fuel language. While COP 31 made some progress on old pathways, such as the Just Transition agreement, it is perplexing that the delegations could not make progress on the other big prong of negotiations: climate finance. The increase in solar panel installations and the significant shift towards battery use in grid storage and transport did not come cheap: the cost of the land required for their installation, their intermittent nature of being dependent on weather, grid upgrades all carry costs. It is global markets, imperfectly connected, but connected, that have managed to bring it to this stage over decades. India and China, major fossil emitters, with large, still indigent populations, are also leaders in total clean energy installations. Therefore it stands to reason that developed countries, which have committed to providing climate finance in recognition of their historical emissions, make good on past promises to shoulder the cost of the carbon emissions that are responsible for warming. Economic crises are a feature, and not a bug, of the interconnected financial system enveloping the world and there are, undeniably, challenges to diverting the necessary finance towards countries most vulnerable to climate change impact. However, it is no longer prudent to sweep this under the rug by scuttling experimental approaches — namely carbon capture — as inimical to the broader commitment to eschew fossil fuel. When the primary framework climate agreement was crafted three decades ago, nobody envisaged AI and the drain that data centres portended or the wars that would see the vociferous antagonists of coal immediately shore up their gas reserves. Without honest good-faith dialogue, the COP is at risk of being a sideshow: a mortal blow to multilateralism.

3. 1. Core Context & Background: Rohingya cannot return unless Myanmar turns democratic

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: On November 19, the International Court of Justice held that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. It is for the first time that the court has found any state responsible for the crime. The verdict, with nine votes to six, was not lightly reached. Genocide requires proof of an intent to destroy a group. In the absence of direct evidence of a plan, the court could infer that intent only if it was “the only reasonable inference” from the facts, a high bar to affix responsibility. The facts it accepted are harrowing. In 2017, in what Myanmar’s army called “clearance operations” against the insurgent Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army, at least 10,000 Rohingya were killed, 1,834 raped and 392 villages destroyed in northern Rakhine State. Over 7,00,000 fled to Bangladesh. Then Army chief Min Aung Hlaing, now Myanmar’s “civilian” President, called the “Bengali problem” an “unfinished job”. Myanmar argued that it had only been fighting insurgents or at worst, driving the Rohingya out or punishing them. The court said that the army drew no distinction between fighters and civilians, had no plan to move anyone, fired on fleeing people and killed children on a scale that could not be explained as punishment. Seen alongside decades of discrimination, the evidence pointed to an intent to destroy. The incidents of 2017 were no aberration. The army drove lakhs of Rohingya into Bangladesh in 1978 and 1991-92. The junta stripped the Rohingya of citizenship in 1982 and the state branded them as “foreigners” in Arakan, disenfranchising them in 2015. While the junta’s Bamar-Buddhist vision has oppressed every minority, the Rohingya have been subjected to the most brutality. More than 1.2 million are in Bangladesh, living in dilapidated conditions, made worse due to diminished international aid. The court ordered Myanmar to allow their safe, voluntary and dignified return and to compensate them, but it has no means of enforcing its judgment. Only the UN Security Council can, but it will be subject to vetoes by Myanmar’s backers, China and Russia. On the very day of the verdict, the two joined the U.S. in Shenzhen to declare the “immunities of State officials” of “paramount importance”. Others, India among them, have courted the regime in Naypyitaw regardless, following sham elections that made the junta leader civilian President earlier this year. And Rakhine State, mired in civil war, is now mostly held by the Arakan Army which is accused of atrocities against the Rohingya. Only a truly democratic, federal, plural and peaceful Myanmar can bring the Rohingya home in safety.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: international court or tribunal / Myanmar / Rohingya crisis / crime / armed Forces / sexual assault / Bangladesh / Citizenship / welfare / United Nations / China / Russia / India / democracy

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: The move aims to encourage consensus-based elections, minimise factional differences and poll-related disputes, and promote social harmony at the village level

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Andhra Pradesh government has significantly increased financial incentives for Gram Panchayats, whose members unanimously elect their heads as well as all ward members, in the upcoming 2026 local body polls. The maximum grant has been raised from ₹20 lakh to ₹50 lakh. The move aims to encourage consensus-based elections, minimise factional differences and poll-related disputes, and promote social harmony at the village level. Elections to 13,167 Gram Panchayats across the state will be held in three phases on November 26, 29 and December 2. Villages with a population up to 5,000 will get a ₹15 lakh grant, a population between 5,000 and 10,000 will get a ₹25 lakh grant and those with a population above 10,000 will get upto ₹50 lakh grant, according to an order issued by the Panchayat Raj and Rural Development Department on November 13. The order explicitly clarifies that the scheme must not interfere with any eligible citizen’s statutory right to contest elections or voters’ right to exercise their franchise freely. The incentives apply strictly to the 2026 Gram Panchayat Ordinary Elections and will only be granted after competent election authorities officially declare and certify that both the Sarpanch and all Ward Members were elected unanimously. The grants must be spent exclusively on approved village developmental activities and public welfare works, subject to standard financial, accounting, and audit rules. The enhanced funds will be released in phases during the tenure of the unanimously elected body.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has on November 22 called upon party leaders, Ministers and MLAs to encourage unanimous elections in gram panchayats so villages can capitalise on the promised government incentives and accelerate grassroots development.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: The Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) of Telangana has justified the rejection of an application under the Right to Information (RTI) Act, seeking details of expenditure on publicity and voter-awareness activities related to the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. However, the explanation does not address whether the provision cited by the CEO can legally be used to reject an application.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The CEO issued a rebuttal to the news report, ‘CEO office rejects RTI query about SIR publicity budget and expenditure’, published in these columns on November 21. The statement said the applicant, S.Q. Masood, an RTI activist and co-founder of www.rtilibrary.in, had sought details of expenditure on various publicity activities, including newspaper advertisements, television and radio campaigns, digital and social media outreach, hoardings, banners and pamphlets. “He himself has stated that these are different categories,” the statement said, justifying the rejection under the Clause (3) of Part-III of the Guide on the RTI Act issued on October 5, 2009, which advised the applicants to seek information in respect of one subject only through one RTI application. The statement also disputed Mr. Masood’s contention that public authorities are legally mandated to proactively disclose budget details under Section 4(1)(b)(xi) of the RTI Act. It said the provision related to the budget allocated to each agency and required disclosure within 120 days of the enactment of the Act. Hence, it argued, the applicant’s request did not fall under this provision. However, the clause cited by the CEO is advisory in nature and does not empower Public Information Officers (PIOs) to reject applications on that ground.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In fact, the RTI Act specifically mentions that if bundling multiple unrelated subjects into one application disproportionately diverts a public authority’s resources, the PIO may invoke Section 7(9) to offer the applicant an opportunity to inspect the relevant records instead.
